translations.literal: Li Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue.

translations.idiomatic: (son: Hui)〉

translations.literal: Wang Xian, Hu Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian; Hu Shining.

translations.idiomatic: (son: Chun)〉

translations.idiomatic: (continued)

sentences.zh: 李承勛王以旂范鏓掞王邦瑞

translations.literal: Li Chengxun, Wang Yiqi, Fan Zong, Wang Bangrui.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengxun; Wang Yiqi; Fan Zong; Wang Bangrui.

sentences.zh: （子正國）〉

translations.idiomatic: (son: Zhengguo)〉

sentences.zh: 鄭曉

translations.literal: Zheng Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiao.

sentences.zh: 李鉞，字虔甫，祥符人。

translations.literal: Li Yue, styled Qianfu, was a man of Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yue, styled Qianfu, was a native of Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 9 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 除御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 巡視中城，理河東鹽政，歷有聲績。

translations.literal: He inspected the Central City, managed salt administration east of the River, and throughout had a reputation for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the Central City, administered salt affairs east of the Yellow River, and earned a solid record of achievement at every post.

sentences.zh: 正德改元，天鳴星變。

translations.literal: When the reign title changed to Zhengde, heaven roared and stars shifted.
translations.idiomatic: When the reign title changed to Zhengde, heaven thundered and the stars showed ominous shifts.

sentences.zh: 偕同官陳數事，論中官李興、寧謹、苗逵、高鳳等罪，而請斥尚書李孟抃、都督神英。

translations.literal: Together with colleagues he memorialized on several matters, discussed the crimes of the eunuchs Li Xing, Ning Jin, Miao Kui, Gao Feng and others, and asked that Minister Li Mengbian and Commissioner-in-chief Shen Ying be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Together with his colleagues he memorialized on several matters, charged the eunuchs Li Xing, Ning Jin, Miao Kui, Gao Feng, and others with crimes, and asked that Minister Li Mengbian and Commissioner-in-chief Shen Ying be removed from office.

sentences.zh: 武宗不能用。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor could not employ him.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 以喪歸。

translations.literal: Because of mourning he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 劉瑾惡鉞劾其黨，假他事罰米五百石輸邊。

translations.literal: Liu Jin hated Yue for impeaching his faction; on a pretext of another matter he fined five hundred piculs of grain to be delivered to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jin resented Yue for impeaching his faction and, on a trumped-up charge, fined him five hundred piculs of grain to be sent to the border.

sentences.zh: 瑾敗，起故官，出為鞏昌知府，尋遷四川副使。

translations.literal: When Jin fell, he was raised to his former office, sent out as prefect of Gongchang, and soon transferred to Vice Commissioner of Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jin's fall he was restored to his former post, appointed prefect of Gongchang, and soon promoted to vice commissioner of Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林俊委鉞與副使何珊討敗流賊方四等，賜金加俸。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun entrusted Yue and Vice Commissioner He Shan to campaign against and defeat the roaming bandits Fang Si and others; he was given gold and an increase in salary.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun assigned Yue and Vice Commissioner He Shan to campaign against the roving bandits Fang Si and others; they defeated them, and Yue was rewarded with gold and a raise in salary.

sentences.zh: 遷陜西按察使，擢右僉都御史巡撫山西。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Shaanxi, promoted to Right Assistant Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Shaanxi, then promoted to right assistant censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 寇入白羊口。

translations.literal: The enemy entered Baiyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders entered Baiyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 鉞度宣、大有備，必窺岢嵐、五臺間，乃亟畫戰守。

translations.literal: Yue judged that Xuan and Da were well prepared and the enemy would surely spy out the region between Kelan and Wutai; he therefore urgently drew up plans for battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: Yue judged that with Xuan and Da well prepared, the raiders would surely probe the corridor between Kelan and Wutai, and he urgently drew up plans for both attack and defense.

sentences.zh: 寇果犯岢嵐，鉞與延綏援將安國、杭雄敗之。

translations.literal: The enemy indeed attacked Kelan; Yue, with reinforcing generals from Yan-sui An Guo and Hang Xiong, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders did strike Kelan; Yue, together with the Yan-sui relief generals An Guo and Hang Xiong, defeated them.

sentences.zh: 加俸一級。

translations.literal: His salary was raised one grade.
translations.idiomatic: His salary rank was raised by one grade.

sentences.zh: 尋討平內寇武廷章等。

translations.literal: Soon he campaigned to pacify the internal rebels Wu Tingzhang and others.
translations.idiomatic: He soon pacified the internal rebels Wu Tingzhang and others.

sentences.zh: 召入理院事。

translations.literal: He was summoned to take charge of Censorate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital to direct affairs at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 四年，代金獻民為兵部尚書兼督團營。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he replaced Jin Xianmin as Minister of War, concurrently supervising the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 he replaced Jin Xianmin as minister of war, concurrently directing the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 中官刁永等多所陳乞，帝皆許之。

translations.literal: The eunuchs Diao Yong and others made many petitions for favors, and the emperor granted them all.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Diao Yong and others petitioned for numerous favors, and the emperor granted every request.

sentences.zh: 又錄司禮扶安家八人官錦衣。

translations.literal: He also enrolled eight men from Director of Ceremonial Fu An's household as officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also enrolled eight members of Director of Ceremonials Fu An's household as officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 南京守備已三人，復命卜春添註以往。

translations.literal: Nanjing already had three defenders; he again ordered Bu Chun added and sent there.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing already had three garrison commanders, yet the emperor again ordered Bu Chun added and dispatched there.

sentences.zh: 禦馬監閻洪因軍政，請自考騰驤四衛及牧馬所官。

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Horse Directorate Yan Hong, citing military administration, asked that officials of the Tengxiang Four Guards and horse-pasturing offices examine themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Hong, director of the Imperial Stud, citing military administration, asked that officials of the Tengxiang Four Guards and the horse-pasturing offices be subject to examination.

sentences.zh: 鉞累疏力爭，帝皆不納，至責以抗旨，令對狀。

translations.literal: Yue repeatedly memorialized in strong opposition; the emperor rejected all, finally rebuked him for resisting the imperial will, and ordered him to answer at court.
translations.idiomatic: Yue memorialized repeatedly in strong opposition; the emperor rejected every plea, finally rebuked him for defying the imperial will, and ordered him to answer for it at court.

sentences.zh: 鉞引罪乃罷。

translations.literal: Yue took blame upon himself and only then was the matter dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Yue accepted blame, and only then was the matter dropped.

sentences.zh: 武定侯郭勛以會武宴列尚書下，疏爭之。

translations.literal: Marquis Guo Xun of Wuding, because at the Military Review banquet he was ranked below ministers, memorialized in protest.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Guo Xun of Wuding, finding himself seated below ministers at the Military Review banquet, memorialized in protest.

sentences.zh: 鉞言：「中府官之有會武宴，猶禮部之有恩榮宴也。

translations.literal: Yue said: "When Central Government offices hold the Military Review banquet, it is like the Ministry of Rites holding the Grace-and-Honor banquet.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "When the central government offices hold the Military Review banquet, it is like the Ministry of Rites holding the Grace-and-Honor banquet.

sentences.zh: 恩榮，禮部為主，會武，中府為主，故皆列諸尚書之次。

translations.literal: For Grace-and-Honor the Ministry of Rites presides; for Military Review the Central Government presides—therefore in both cases they are listed after all ministers.
translations.idiomatic: For Grace-and-Honor the Ministry of Rites presides; for Military Review the central government presides—so in both cases they are listed immediately after the ministers.

sentences.zh: 宴圖可征，不得引團營故事。

translations.literal: Banquet diagrams can verify this; one cannot cite Regiment Camp precedents.
translations.idiomatic: Seating diagrams of the banquets prove the point; one cannot invoke Regiment Camp precedents.

sentences.zh: 」帝竟從勛言。

translations.literal: " The emperor in the end followed Xun's view.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ultimately sided with Xun.

sentences.zh: 錦衣革職百戶李全奏乞復任，鉞請治其違旨罪，帝不問。

translations.literal: Li Quan, a cashiered hundred-household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, memorialized asking restoration; Yue asked that he be punished for violating the imperial will; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan, a cashiered hundred-household of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard, petitioned to be restored to office; Yue asked that he be punished for defying the imperial will, but the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 於是官旗鄭彪等皆援全例以請，鉞執奏如初，而疏有「猿攀狐媚」語。

translations.literal: Thereupon guard officers Zheng Biao and others all cited Quan's precedent in petitioning; Yue held to his original memorial, and in the memorial used the phrase "apes climbing and foxes fawning."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon guard officers such as Zheng Biao all cited Quan's case in their petitions; Yue held firm to his original memorial, which used the phrase "apes climbing and foxes fawning."

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，復責對狀，奪俸一月。

translations.literal: The emperor disliked it, again ordered him to answer at court, and docked one month's salary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took offense, again ordered him to answer at court, and docked one month's salary.

sentences.zh: 鉞既屢諫不用，失上意，且知為近幸所嫉。

translations.literal: Yue had remonstrated repeatedly without being employed, lost the emperor's favor, and moreover knew he was envied by those close to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Yue had remonstrated again and again without effect, had lost the emperor's favor, and knew he was detested by those close to the throne.

sentences.zh: 會病，遂再疏乞休，許馳驛，未行，卒。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, he then twice memorialized begging retirement; permission was granted to travel by relay horse; before he set out, he died.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he twice memorialized begging retirement; permission was granted to travel by relay post; before he could depart, he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，遣官護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; officials were dispatched to escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior tutor of the heir apparent, and officials were dispatched to escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 久之，賜謚恭簡。

translations.literal: After a long time he was granted the posthumous title Gongjian.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he was granted the posthumous title Gongjian (Respectful and Simple).

sentences.zh: 子惠，正德十二年進士，官行人。

translations.literal: His son Hui, a jinshi of the twelfth year of Zhengde, served as courier.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui passed the jinshi in Zhengde year 12 and served as a courier.

sentences.zh: 諫武宗南巡，死於廷杖。

translations.literal: He remonstrated against the Martial Emperor's southern tour and died under the court bastinado.
translations.idiomatic: He remonstrated against the Martial Emperor's southern tour and died under the palace bastinado.

sentences.zh: 贈監察御史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 王憲，字維綱，東平人。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, styled Weigang, was a man of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, styled Weigang, was a native of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年進士。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 3 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 歷知阜平、滑二縣。

translations.literal: He successively served as magistrate of Fuping and Hua counties.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as magistrate of Fuping and Hua counties.

sentences.zh: 召拜御史。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 正德初，擢大理寺丞。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengde he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign he was promoted to vice director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 遷右僉都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Assistant Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right assistant censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 清理甘肅屯田。

translations.literal: He cleared and settled the garrison fields of Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the reclaimed garrison fields of Gansu.

sentences.zh: 進右副都御史，巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Right Vice Censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 歷鄖陽、大同。

translations.literal: He served in Xiangyang and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as grand coordinator in Xiangyang and Datong.

sentences.zh: 以應州禦寇功，蔭錦衣，世百戶。

translations.literal: For merit in resisting the enemy at Yingzhou, his descendant was ennobled in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred generations as hundred-household.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in resisting the enemy at Yingzhou, a descendant was ennobled in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard as hereditary hundred-household.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部右侍郎，改撫陜西，入為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Minister of Revenue, changed to grand coordinator of Shaanxi, and entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to right vice minister of revenue, then reassigned as grand coordinator of Shaanxi, and later entered the capital as right vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 近畿盜起，偕太監張忠、都督朱泰捕之，復以功蔭錦衣。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in the capital vicinity; together with eunuch Zhang Zhong and Commissioner-in-chief Zhu Tai he captured them, and again for merit his descendant was ennobled in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in the capital region, he joined eunuch Zhang Zhong and Commissioner-in-chief Zhu Tai in suppressing them and again earned a hereditary ennoblement in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard.

sentences.zh: 武宗南征，命率戶、兵、工三部郎各一人督理軍儲。

translations.literal: When the Martial Emperor made his southern campaign, he was ordered to lead one official each from the ministries of Revenue, War, and Works to supervise military stores.
translations.idiomatic: During the Martial Emperor's southern campaign he was ordered to lead one director from each of the ministries of Revenue, War, and Works in supervising military supplies.

sentences.zh: 駕旋，以中旨代王瓊為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, by secret edict he replaced Wang Qiong as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial procession returned, a secret edict replaced Wang Qiong with him as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，為給事中史道劾罷。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, he was impeached and dismissed by supervising secretary Shi Dao.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, supervising secretary Shi Dao impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四年，廷推鄧璋及憲為三邊總制，言官持不可，帝竟用憲。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiajing, at court they recommended Deng Zhang and Xian for the Three Borders command; censorial officials held it impossible, but the emperor ultimately used Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 4 the court recommended Deng Zhang and Xian for the Three Borders command; censorial officials objected, but the emperor appointed Xian after all.

sentences.zh: 部將王宰、史經連敗寇，璽書褒諭。

translations.literal: Deputy generals Wang Zai and Shi Jing repeatedly defeated the enemy; imperial letters praised him.
translations.idiomatic: His deputies Wang Zai and Shi Jing repeatedly defeated the enemy, and the emperor sent sealed letters of praise.

sentences.zh: 吉囊數萬騎渡河從石臼墩深入，憲督總兵官鄭卿、杭雄、趙瑛等分據要害擊之，都指揮卜雲斷其歸路。

translations.literal: Ji's raiders, tens of thousands of horsemen, crossed the river and penetrated deeply by way of Shijiudun; Xian supervised the commander-in-chief Zheng Qing, Hang Xiong, Zhao Ying and others in holding key points to strike them, and Commander Bu Yun cut their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's horsemen, tens of thousands strong, crossed the river and drove deep inland by way of Shijiudun; Xian directed the commander-in-chief Zheng Qing, Hang Xiong, Zhao Ying, and others to seize key positions and strike them, while Commander Bu Yun cut off their retreat.

sentences.zh: 寇至青羊嶺，大敗去。

translations.literal: When the enemy reached Qingyang Ridge they were greatly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingyang Ridge the raiders suffered a crushing defeat and fled.

sentences.zh: 五日四捷，斬首三百余級，獲馬駝器仗無算。

translations.literal: In five days four victories; over three hundred heads were cut; horses, camels, weapons and gear beyond counting were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In five days they won four victories, took more than three hundred heads, and captured horses, camels, weapons, and equipment beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜，加憲太子太保，復予一子蔭。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted Xian to Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent, and again granted one descendant ennoblement.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased, promoted Xian to junior preceptor of the heir apparent, and again granted one descendant an ennoblement.

sentences.zh: 至是，凡三蔭錦衣世百戶矣。

translations.literal: By then, in all he had been ennobled in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard for one hundred generations three times.
translations.idiomatic: By then he had received three hereditary ennoblements in the Embroidered-Uniform Guard as hundred-household.

sentences.zh: 中官織花絨於陜，憲請罷之。

translations.literal: Eunuchs wove patterned velvet in Shaanxi; Xian asked that it be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: When eunuchs wove patterned velvet in Shaanxi, Xian petitioned to have the practice abolished.

sentences.zh: 又因九廟成，請釋還議禮得罪者，頗為士大夫所稱。

translations.literal: Also when the Nine Temples were completed, he asked that those punished in the Rites Controversy be released and returned—acts much praised by scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nine Temples were completed he also asked that those punished in the Rites Controversy be released—acts that won him considerable praise among scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 張璁、桂萼欲用王瓊為總制，乃改憲南京兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Zhang Cong and Gui E wished to use Wang Qiong as border commander; Xian was therefore changed to Minister of War at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cong and Gui E wished to appoint Wang Qiong as border commander, so Xian was transferred to minister of war at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 已，入為左都御史。

translations.literal: Before long he entered as Left Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he entered the capital as left censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 朔州告急，廷推憲總督宣、大。

translations.literal: Shuozhou reported emergency; at court they recommended Xian as supreme commander of Xuan and Da.
translations.idiomatic: When Shuozhou reported an emergency, the court recommended Xian as supreme commander of Xuan and Da.

sentences.zh: 憲不肯行，曰：「我甫入中臺，何見驅亟也。

translations.literal: Xian refused to go, saying: "I have only just entered the Central Secretariat—why am I being driven out so hastily?
translations.idiomatic: Xian refused to go, saying, "I have only just entered the Central Secretariat—why am I being hustled out so soon?

sentences.zh: 」給事中夏言、趙廷瑞劾憲托疾避難，復罷歸。

translations.literal: " Supervising secretaries Xia Yan and Zhao Tingrui impeached Xian for feigning illness to avoid hardship; he was again dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: " Supervising secretaries Xia Yan and Zhao Tingrui impeached Xian for feigning illness to avoid hardship, and he was again dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝追念憲，召為兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor recalled Xian with fondness and summoned him as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor recalled Xian with fondness and summoned him as minister of war.

sentences.zh: 小王子入寇，條上平戎及諸邊防禦事宜。

translations.literal: When the Little Prince raided, he itemized proposals for pacifying the steppe and various border defense measures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Little Prince raided, he submitted detailed proposals for pacifying the steppe and for border defense.

sentences.zh: 又請立京營分伍操練法，諸將不得藉內府供事，規避營操。

translations.literal: He also asked to establish graded drilling for the capital camps, and that generals not use service in the inner palace to evade camp training.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to establish squad-based drill for the capital camps and that generals not use service in the inner palace as a pretext to evade camp training.

sentences.zh: 帝皆嘉納。

translations.literal: The emperor approved all with praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved all of these proposals.

sentences.zh: 舊制，軍功論敘，有生擒、斬首、當先、殿後、奇功、頭功諸等，其後濫冒日多。

translations.literal: Under the old system, military merit was assessed with categories including live capture, decapitation, leading the van, bringing up the rear, extraordinary merit, and foremost merit—but later false claims grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system military merit was assessed in categories including live capture, decapitation, leading the van, bringing up the rear, extraordinary merit, and foremost merit—but false claims grew more common every year.

sentences.zh: 憲定軍功襲替格，自永樂至正德，酌其輕重大小之差，臚析以上。

translations.literal: Xian fixed regulations for hereditary military merit, from Yongle through Zhengde calibrating lighter and heavier differences, and presented an itemized memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Xian drew up regulations for hereditary military merit from the Yongle through the Zhengde reigns, calibrating lighter and heavier distinctions, and presented an itemized memorial.

sentences.zh: 詔著之《會典》為成式。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it written into the Collected Statutes as the established form.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered it written into the Collected Statutes as the established standard.

sentences.zh: 尋兼督團營。

translations.literal: Soon he also concurrently supervised the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also appointed to direct the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 西番諸國來貢，稱王號者百余人。

translations.literal: Western barbarian states came in tribute; over a hundred persons styled themselves with kingly titles.
translations.idiomatic: Western Tibetan states came to offer tribute, and more than a hundred persons styled themselves kings.

sentences.zh: 憲與禮臣夏言等請如成化、弘治間例，答敕止國王一人，仍限貢期、人數。

translations.literal: Xian, with Minister of Rites Xia Yan and others, asked that per the precedents of Chenghua and Hongzhi only one king be acknowledged in the reply edict, while tribute periods and personnel be reimposed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, together with Minister of Rites Xia Yan and others, asked that, following the precedents of the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, the reply edict acknowledge only one king and that tribute periods and personnel quotas be reimposed.

sentences.zh: 議乃定。

translations.literal: The deliberation was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: The policy was then settled.

sentences.zh: 大同兵變，憲初言首亂當誅，余宜散遣。

translations.literal: When the Datong troops mutinied, Xian initially said the ringleaders should be executed and the rest dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: When the Datong troops mutinied, Xian initially argued that the ringleaders should be executed and the rest dispersed.

sentences.zh: 而大學士張孚敬與總督劉源清力主用兵，憲乃不敢堅前議。

translations.literal: But Grand Secretary Zhang Fojing with Grand Coordinator Liu Yuanqing strongly favored military action; Xian then dared not hold to his earlier view.
translations.idiomatic: But Grand Secretary Zhang Fojing and Grand Coordinator Liu Yuanqing strongly favored military action, and Xian then dared not hold to his earlier view.

sentences.zh: 源清攻城不能下，北寇又內侵，請別遣大臣禦北寇，己得專攻城。

translations.literal: Yuanqing besieged the city without success; northern raiders again invaded within; he asked that another minister be separately sent against the northern raiders so he could devote himself to the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing besieged the city without success; northern raiders invaded again from within; he asked that another minister be dispatched against the northern raiders so that he could devote himself to the siege.

sentences.zh: 憲亦議從其奏，論者多尤憲。

translations.literal: Xian also approved this in council; many critics blamed Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Xian also approved this proposal in council, and many critics blamed him.

sentences.zh: 會帝悟大同重鎮，不宜破壞，乃寢其事，亂亦旋定。

translations.literal: But the emperor came to see that Datong was a vital strongpoint and must not be destroyed; the matter was shelved, and the disturbance soon subsided.
translations.idiomatic: But the emperor came to see that Datong was a vital strongpoint and must not be destroyed; the matter was shelved, and the disturbance soon subsided.

sentences.zh: 源清竟得罪去。

translations.literal: Yuanqing in the end was punished and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanqing in the end was punished and left office.

sentences.zh: 居數年，憲引年歸，卒。

translations.literal: After several years Xian cited age and returned home; he died.
translations.idiomatic: After several years Xian cited his age and retired home, where he died.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚康毅。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and granted the title Kangyi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian and granted the title Kangyi (Healthy and Resolute).

sentences.zh: 子汝孝，副都御史。

translations.literal: His son Ruxiao became Vice Censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ruxiao rose to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 見《丁汝夔傳》。

translations.literal: See the biography of Ding Ruokui.
translations.idiomatic: See the biography of Ding Ruokui.

sentences.zh: 胡世寧，字永清，仁和人。

translations.literal: Hu Shining, styled Yongqing, was a man of Renhe.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shining, styled Yongqing, was a native of Renhe.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Hongzhi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi year 6 he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 性剛直，不畏強禦，且知兵。

translations.literal: By nature he was upright and unyielding, feared no powerful oppressor, and moreover understood military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was upright and fearless before the powerful, and he also understood military affairs.

sentences.zh: 除德安推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating magistrate of De'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating magistrate of De'an.

sentences.zh: 岐王初就藩，從官驕，世寧裁之。

translations.literal: When Prince Qi first went to his fief, his attendants were arrogant; Shining restrained them.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Qi first went to his fief, his attendants were arrogant; Shining reined them in.

sentences.zh: 他日復請湖田，持不可。

translations.literal: Another day they again asked for lake fields; he held firm that it could not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On another occasion they again petitioned for lake fields; he firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 遷南京刑部主事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to a directorship in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 應詔陳邊備十策，復上書極言時政闕失。

translations.literal: In response to an edict he presented ten policies on border defense, and again memorialized at length on failures of current administration.
translations.idiomatic: In response to an imperial edict he presented ten policies on border defense, and again memorialized at length on the failures of current administration.

sentences.zh: 時孝宗已不豫，猶頷之。

translations.literal: At the time Xiaozong was already gravely ill, yet still nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiaozong was already gravely ill, yet he still nodded his approval.

sentences.zh: 再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to director.

sentences.zh: 與李承勛、魏校、余祐善，時稱「南都四君子」。

translations.literal: Together with Li Chengxun, Wei Xiao, and Yu Youshan, he was at the time called "the Four Gentlemen of the Southern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: Together with Li Chengxun, Wei Xiao, and Yu Youshan, he was known at the time as the Four Gentlemen of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 遷廣西太平知府。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prefect of Taiping in Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed prefect of Taiping in Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 太平知州李濬數殺掠吏民，世寧密檄龍英知州趙元瑤擒之。

translations.literal: Taiping prefect Li Jun repeatedly killed and plundered officials and people; Shining secretly dispatched an order to Longying prefect Zhao Yuanyao to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping prefect Li Jun repeatedly killed and plundered officials and commoners; Shining secretly ordered Longying prefect Zhao Yuanyao to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 思明叛族黃文昌四世殺知府，占三州二十七村。

translations.literal: The rebel clan of Huang Wenchang in Siming, for four generations having killed prefects, occupied three prefectures and twenty-seven villages.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Huang Wenchang clan of Siming had killed prefects for four generations and occupied three prefectures and twenty-seven villages.

sentences.zh: 副總兵康泰偕世寧入思明，執其兄弟三人。

translations.literal: Vice commander-in-chief Kang Tai together with Shining entered Siming and seized three of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commander-in-chief Kang Tai entered Siming with Shining and seized three of Wenchang's brothers.

sentences.zh: 而泰畏文昌夜遁，委世寧空城中，危甚。

translations.literal: But Tai feared Wenchang and fled by night, leaving Shining in an empty city—extremely perilous.
translations.idiomatic: But Kang Tai, fearing Wenchang, fled by night and left Shining alone in an empty city—a situation of grave danger.

sentences.zh: 諸土酋德世寧，發兵援，乃得還。

translations.literal: The native chieftains were grateful to Shining, raised troops to aid him, and only then could he return.
translations.idiomatic: The native chieftains, who respected Shining, raised troops to rescue him, and only then was he able to return.

sentences.zh: 文昌懼，歸所侵地，降。

translations.literal: Wenchang was afraid, returned the land he had seized, and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Wenchang, in fear, returned the seized territories and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 土官承襲，長吏率要賄不時奏，以故諸酋怨叛。

translations.literal: When native officials inherited office, senior officials as a rule demanded bribes and did not memorialize in timely fashion; for this reason the chieftains resented and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When native officials inherited their posts, senior officials routinely demanded bribes and failed to report succession in timely fashion; for this reason the chieftains grew resentful and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 世寧令：「生子即聞府。

translations.literal: Shining ordered: "When a son is born, immediately notify the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shining ordered, "When a son is born, the prefecture must be notified at once.

sentences.zh: 應世及者，年十歲以上，朔望謁府。

translations.literal: Those who should succeed, from age ten upward, shall attend the prefecture on the first and fifteenth of the month.
translations.idiomatic: Heirs from age ten upward shall attend the prefecture on the first and fifteenth of each month.

sentences.zh: 父兄有故，按籍請官於朝。

translations.literal: When father or elder brother has cause, according to the register request office from the court.
translations.idiomatic: When a father or elder brother dies or is removed, succession shall be requested from the court according to the register.

sentences.zh: 」土官大悅。

translations.literal: " The native officials were greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " The native officials were greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 母喪歸。

translations.literal: On his mother's death he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home upon his mother's death.

sentences.zh: 服闋赴京。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he went to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended he traveled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 道滄州，流寇攻城急。

translations.literal: Passing through Cangzhou, roaming bandits pressed the siege of the city urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Cangzhou, he found roving bandits pressing a fierce assault on the city.

sentences.zh: 世寧即馳入城，畫防守計。

translations.literal: Shining immediately galloped into the city and drew up plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shining immediately rode into the city and drew up a defensive plan.

sentences.zh: 賊攻七日夜，不能拔，引去。

translations.literal: The bandits attacked seven days and nights, could not take it, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits attacked for seven days and nights, failed to take the city, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 再知寶慶府。

translations.literal: He again served as prefect of Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed prefect of Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 岷王及鎮守中官王潤皆嚴憚之。

translations.literal: Prince Min of Min and the garrison eunuch Wang Run all feared him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Min and the garrison eunuch Wang Run both stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 遷江西副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 與都御史俞諫畫策擒盜，討平王浩八。

translations.literal: Together with Censor-in-chief Yu Jian he plotted to capture bandits and campaigned to pacify Wang Haoba.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Censor-in-chief Yu Jian he devised a plan to capture the bandits and pacified Wang Haoba.

sentences.zh: 以暇城廣昌、南豐、新城。

translations.literal: In his spare time he walled Guangchang, Nanfeng, and Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: In intervals between campaigns he fortified Guangchang, Nanfeng, and Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 當是時，寧王宸濠驕橫有異志，莫敢言，世寧憤甚。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Ning Zhu Chenhao was arrogant and overbearing with rebellious intent; none dared speak; Shining was deeply indignant.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, was arrogant and harbored rebellious ambitions; no one dared speak out, and Shining was deeply indignant.

sentences.zh: 正德九年三月上疏曰：「江西之盜，剿撫二說相持，臣愚以為無難決也。

translations.literal: In the third month of the ninth year of Zhengde he memorialized: "The bandits of Jiangxi—suppression and pacification, the two views contend; this subject in his folly thinks there is no difficulty in deciding.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Zhengde year 9 he memorialized, "As for the bandits of Jiangxi, the debate between suppression and pacification has dragged on; in my humble view the matter is not hard to decide.

sentences.zh: 已撫者不誅，再叛者毋赦，初起者亟剿，如是而已。

translations.literal: Those already pacified should not be executed; those who rebel again should not be pardoned; those newly risen should be swiftly suppressed—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Those already pacified should not be executed; those who rebel again should receive no pardon; those just arising should be swiftly suppressed—that is all.

sentences.zh: 顧江西患非盜賊。

translations.literal: But Jiangxi's affliction is not bandits.
translations.idiomatic: But Jiangxi's true affliction is not banditry.

sentences.zh: 寧府威日張，不逞之徒群聚而導以非法，上下諸司承奉太過。

translations.literal: The Ning princely establishment's power grows daily; unruly men gather in groups and lead it into unlawful acts; superior and subordinate offices all serve it excessively.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning's power grows daily; unruly men gather around him and lead him into unlawful acts, while offices at every level defer to him far too readily.

sentences.zh: 數假火災奪民廛地，采辦擾旁郡，蹂籍遍窮鄉。

translations.literal: Repeatedly under pretext of fire disasters they seize commoners' market lands; procurement missions disturb neighboring prefectures; trampling extends through every poor village.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again, under pretext of fire disasters, they seize commoners' market lands; procurement missions disturb neighboring prefectures; and their depredations reach into the poorest villages.

sentences.zh: 臣恐良民不安，皆起為盜。

translations.literal: Your subject fears that good people, unsettled, will all rise as bandits.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that law-abiding people, driven to desperation, will all turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 臣下畏禍，多懷二心，禮樂刑政漸不自朝廷出矣。

translations.literal: Officials fear disaster, many harbor divided hearts; rites, music, punishments and administration gradually no longer issue from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Officials fear retribution and many harbor divided loyalties; rites, music, punishments, and administration are gradually ceasing to issue from the court.

sentences.zh: 請於都御史俞諫、任漢中專委一人，或別選公忠大臣鎮撫。

translations.literal: I ask that among Censor-in-chief Yu Jian and Ren Hanzhong one be specially entrusted, or that another loyal and upright great minister be chosen to pacify and oversee.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that either Censor-in-chief Yu Jian or Ren Hanzhong be given sole responsibility, or that another loyal and upright senior minister be chosen to oversee and pacify the region.

sentences.zh: 敕王止治其國，毋撓有司，以靖亂源，銷意外變。

translations.literal: Command the prince to govern only his state, not disturb the regular offices, thereby quieting the source of disorder and dispelling unforeseen change.
translations.idiomatic: Command the prince to govern only his own domain and not interfere with civil officials, so as to quiet the source of disorder and forestall unforeseen upheaval.

sentences.zh: 」章下兵部。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent down to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was referred to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 尚書陸完議，令諫往計賊情撫剿之宜，至所言違制擾民，疑出偽托，宜令王約束之。

translations.literal: Minister Lu Wan deliberated: order Jian to go assess bandit conditions and the suitability of pacification or suppression; as for the statements of violation of regulations and disturbing the people, suspecting they came from false impersonation, the prince should be ordered to restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Lu Wan proposed that Jian be sent to assess bandit conditions and decide between pacification and suppression; as for the charges of violating regulations and disturbing the people, he suspected forgery and recommended that the prince be ordered to restrain his followers.

sentences.zh: 得旨報可。

translations.literal: Imperial assent was received and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial approval was granted.

sentences.zh: 宸濠聞，大怒。

translations.literal: Chenhao heard and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao heard of this and was furious.

sentences.zh: 列世寧罪，遍賂權幸，必殺世寧。

translations.literal: He listed Shining's crimes, bribed powerful favorites everywhere, and vowed to kill Shining.
translations.idiomatic: He drew up charges against Shining, bribed powerful favorites throughout the court, and resolved to have him killed.

sentences.zh: 章下都察院。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent down to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 右都御史李士實，宸濠黨也，與左都御史石玠等上言，世寧狂率當治。

translations.literal: Right Censor-in-chief Li Shishi, Chenhao's partisan, together with Left Censor-in-chief Shi Jie and others memorialized that Shining was reckless and should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Right Censor-in-chief Li Shishi, a partisan of Chenhao, joined Left Censor-in-chief Shi Jie and others in memorializing that Shining was reckless and should be punished.

sentences.zh: 命未下，宸濠奏復至，指世寧為妖言。

translations.literal: Before the order was issued, Chenhao's memorial again arrived, denouncing Shining for sorcerous speech.
translations.idiomatic: Before the order was issued, another memorial from Chenhao arrived, denouncing Shining for sedition and sorcery.

sentences.zh: 乃命錦衣官校逮捕世寧。

translations.literal: Thereupon officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard were ordered to arrest Shining.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered officers of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard to arrest Shining.

sentences.zh: 世寧已遷福建按察使，取道還裏。

translations.literal: Shining had already been transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian and was taking the route home.
translations.idiomatic: Shining had already been transferred to surveillance commissioner of Fujian and was traveling home by a circuitous route.

sentences.zh: 宸濠遂誣世寧逃，馳使令浙江巡按潘鵬執送江西。

translations.literal: Chenhao then falsely charged that Shining had fled, dispatched a fast messenger ordering Zhejiang investigating censor Pan Peng to seize and send him to Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao then falsely claimed that Shining had fled and dispatched a fast courier ordering Zhejiang investigating censor Pan Peng to seize him and send him to Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 鵬盡系世寧家人，索之急。

translations.literal: Peng imprisoned all of Shining's family and pressed the search urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Peng imprisoned all of Shining's family and pressed the search urgently.

sentences.zh: 李承勛為按察使，保護之。

translations.literal: Li Chengxun was surveillance commissioner and protected him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengxun, who was surveillance commissioner, protected him.

sentences.zh: 世寧乃亡命抵京師，自投錦衣獄。

translations.literal: Shining then fled for his life to the capital and surrendered himself to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison.
translations.idiomatic: Shining then fled to the capital and surrendered himself to the Embroidered-Uniform Guard prison.

sentences.zh: 獄中三上書言宸濠逆狀，卒不省。

translations.literal: In prison he thrice memorialized on Chenhao's rebellious conduct; in the end it was not understood.
translations.idiomatic: From prison he memorialized three times on Chenhao's treasonous conduct, but the court took no notice.

sentences.zh: 系歲餘，言官程啟充、徐文華、蕭鳴鳳、邢寰等交章救，楊一清復以危言動錢寧，乃謫戍瀋陽。

translations.literal: Imprisoned over a year, remonstrating officials Cheng Qichong, Xu Wenhua, Xiao Mingfeng, Xing Huan and others memorialized in succession to save him; Yang Yiqing again used alarming words to move Qian Ning; he was then banished to garrison duty at Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year in prison, remonstrating officials including Cheng Qichong, Xu Wenhua, Xiao Mingfeng, and Xing Huan memorialized in succession on his behalf; Yang Yiqing again used alarming words to move Qian Ning; and Shining was banished to garrison duty at Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 既免喪家居，朝廷方議「大禮」，異議者多得罪。

translations.literal: After mourning ended he dwelt at home; the court was then debating the "Great Rites"; many who dissented were punished.
translations.idiomatic: After his mourning ended he lived at home while the court debated the Great Rites; many who dissented were punished.

sentences.zh: 世寧意是張璁等，疏乞早定追崇「大禮」。

translations.literal: Shining's view agreed with Zhang Cong and others; he memorialized begging early settlement of posthumous honors for the "Great Rites."
translations.idiomatic: Shining sided with Zhang Cong and others and memorialized asking that the Great Rites be settled promptly.

sentences.zh: 未上，語聞京師。

translations.literal: Before it was submitted, word reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could submit it, word of his views reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 既有議遷顯陵祔天壽山者，世寧極言不可，乃並前疏上之。

translations.literal: When there was discussion of moving the Xian Mausoleum to be enshrined at Tianshou Mountain, Shining strongly said it could not be; he then submitted the earlier memorial together.
translations.idiomatic: When some proposed moving the Xian Mausoleum to be enshrined at Mount Tianshou, Shining strongly objected and then submitted his earlier memorial together with this protest.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉嘆。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him deeply.

sentences.zh: 無何，聞廷臣伏闕爭，有杖死者，馳疏言：「臣向以仁、明、武三言進，然尤以仁為本。

translations.literal: Before long, hearing that court officials prostrated themselves at the palace gate in protest and some died under the bastinado, he sent a hurried memorial: "Your subject formerly advanced the three words benevolence, clarity, and martial prowess, yet especially took benevolence as root.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, hearing that court officials had prostrated themselves at the palace gate in protest and that some had died under the bastinado, he sent an urgent memorial: "Your subject formerly advanced the three principles of benevolence, clarity, and martial prowess, yet took benevolence above all as the foundation.

sentences.zh: 仁，生成之德；

translations.literal: Benevolence is the virtue of generating and nurturing;
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence is the virtue that generates and nurtures;

sentences.zh: 明，日月之臨，皆不可一日無。

translations.literal: clarity is the sun and moon's shining—neither can be absent for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: clarity is the sun and moon's shining over the realm—neither can be absent for a single day.

sentences.zh: 武則雷霆之威，但可一震而已。

translations.literal: Martial prowess is thunder's majesty—it suffices to shake once.
translations.idiomatic: Martial prowess is the thunder's awe—it need only strike once.

sentences.zh: 今廷臣忤旨，陛下赫然示威，辱以箠楚，體羸弱者輒斃。

translations.literal: Now court officials offend the imperial will; Your Majesty suddenly displays might, humiliates them with flogging; those weak in body promptly die.
translations.idiomatic: Now court officials have offended the imperial will; Your Majesty has suddenly displayed wrath, humiliated them with the rod, and those of frail constitution have died on the spot.

sentences.zh: 傳之天下，書之史冊，謂鞭撲行殿陛，刑辱及士夫，非所以光聖德。

translations.literal: Spread through the realm, written in the historical records—that flogging was carried out on the palace steps, that punishment and humiliation reached scholar-officials—is not the way to glorify sagely virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When this spreads through the realm and is written in the historical records—that the rod was applied on the palace steps and that punishment and humiliation reached scholar-officials—it will not glorify Your Majesty's sagely virtue.

sentences.zh: 新進一言偶合，後難保必當；

translations.literal: A newly risen man's one word may by chance agree—later it is hard to guarantee he will always be right;
translations.idiomatic: A newly risen man may happen to speak words that accord with Your Majesty's wish, yet later one cannot guarantee he will always be right;

sentences.zh: 舊德老成，一事偶忤，後未必皆非。

translations.literal: an old worthy of mature virtue, on one matter by chance offending, later is not necessarily always wrong.
translations.idiomatic: while a seasoned elder who offends on one matter is not necessarily always wrong thereafter.

sentences.zh: 望陛下以三無私之心，照臨於上，無先存適莫於中。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty, with the three kinds of selflessness in heart, shine illumination from above, and not beforehand harbor favor or disfavor within.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty, with a heart free of private bias in all three respects, will shine illumination from above and not harbor predetermined favor or disfavor within.

sentences.zh: 」帝雖不能從，亦不忤。

translations.literal: " The emperor though unable to follow, was not offended.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, though unable to follow his advice, was not offended.

sentences.zh: 尋召為兵部左侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as left vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 條戍邊時所見險塞利害二十五事以上。

translations.literal: He itemized twenty-five matters of strategic passes, dangers and benefits seen while garrisoning the border, and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twenty-five items on the strategic passes, dangers, and advantages he had observed while serving on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又請善保聖躬，毋輕餌藥物。

translations.literal: He also asked that the sacred person be well preserved and medicines not lightly taken.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the emperor guard his health carefully and not lightly take medicines.

sentences.zh: 獻《大學·秦誓》章、《洪範》「惟辟威福」、《系辭·節》「初爻」講義，並乞留中。

translations.literal: He presented exegeses on the "Qin Oath" chapter of the Great Learning, on "Only the sovereign has majesty and blessing" from the Hongfan, and on the "First line" section of the Xici, and asked that all be kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He presented exegeses on the "Qin Oath" chapter of the Great Learning, on "Only the sovereign possesses majesty and blessing" from the Hongfan, and on the "First line" of the Appended Remarks, and asked that all be kept within the palace.

sentences.zh: 給事中余經遂劾世寧啟告密之漸。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Yu Jing then impeached Shining for opening the gradual slide toward secret denunciations.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Yu Jing then impeached Shining for encouraging the gradual slide toward secret denunciations.

sentences.zh: 世寧乞罷，不許。

translations.literal: Shining begged dismissal; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shining asked to resign; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 「大禮」成，進秩一等。

translations.literal: When the "Great Rites" were settled, his rank was advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: When the Great Rites were settled, his rank was advanced one grade.

sentences.zh: 復陳用人二十事。

translations.literal: He again presented twenty matters on employing men.
translations.idiomatic: He again presented twenty proposals on the employment of officials.

sentences.zh: 工匠趙奎等五十四人以中官請，悉授職。

translations.literal: Fifty-four artisans including Zhao Kui, at eunuchs' request, were all granted offices.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty-four artisans including Zhao Kui were all granted offices at the eunuchs' request.

sentences.zh: 世寧言賞過濫，不納。

translations.literal: Shining said rewards were excessive; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Shining said the rewards were excessive; the emperor did not accept his view.

sentences.zh: 屢疏引疾。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized citing illness.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized citing illness.

sentences.zh: 改南京吏部，就遷工部尚書。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then promptly transferred to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then promptly promoted to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 已，復召為左都御史，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as Left Censor-in-chief, with addition of Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was again summoned as left censor-in-chief and made junior tutor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 辭宮銜，許之。

translations.literal: He declined the palace title; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined the palace title, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 世寧故方嚴。

translations.literal: Shining had formerly been stern and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Shining had formerly been stern and severe.

sentences.zh: 及掌憲，務持大體。

translations.literal: When he took charge of the Censorate, he strove to uphold the larger principles.
translations.idiomatic: When he took charge of the Censorate, he strove to uphold the larger principles.

sentences.zh: 條上憲綱十余條，末言：「近士習忌刻，一遭讒毀，則終身廢棄。

translations.literal: He itemized more than ten articles of censorial regulations, ending: "Recently scholar-officials' custom is jealous severity; once slandered, they are abandoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted more than ten articles on censorial regulations, ending with: "Recently the custom among scholar-officials has grown jealous and severe; once slandered, a man is abandoned for life.

sentences.zh: 僉事彭祺發豪強罪，受謗奪官。

translations.literal: Associate Administration Vice Commissioner Peng Qi exposed powerful families' crimes, suffered slander and lost office.
translations.idiomatic: Associate administration vice commissioner Peng Qi exposed the crimes of powerful families, was slandered, and lost his office.

sentences.zh: 諸如此者，宜許大臣申理。

translations.literal: Cases such as these ought to allow great ministers to plead on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In cases such as these, great ministers ought to be allowed to plead on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 」帝采其言，惟祺報寢。

translations.literal: " The emperor adopted his words, only Qi's report was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor adopted his advice in general, but Peng Qi's case alone was shelved.

sentences.zh: 執政請禁私謁，世寧曰：「臣官以察為名。

translations.literal: The chief ministers asked to forbid private audiences; Shining said: "Your subject's office takes investigation as its name.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers asked to forbid private audiences; Shining said, "Your subject's office is named for investigation.

sentences.zh: 人非接其貌，聽其言，無由悉其才行。

translations.literal: Unless one meets a man's appearance and hears his words, there is no means to know fully his conduct and ability.
translations.idiomatic: Unless one meets a man face to face and hears him speak, there is no way to know his conduct and ability fully.

sentences.zh: 」帝以為然，遂弗禁。

translations.literal: " The emperor thought it correct, and therefore did not forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed and did not forbid private audiences.

sentences.zh: 俄改刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 每重獄，別白為帝言之，帝輒感悟。

translations.literal: Whenever there was a grave case, he clarified and explained it to the emperor; the emperor would then be moved to understanding.
translations.idiomatic: In every grave case he clarified the facts for the emperor, who was invariably moved to understanding.

sentences.zh: 中官剛聰誣漕卒掠禦服，坐二千人，世寧劾其妄。

translations.literal: The eunuch Gang Cong falsely charged grain-transport soldiers with plundering imperial garments; two thousand men were implicated; Shining impeached the falsity.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Gang Cong falsely accused grain-transport soldiers of plundering imperial garments and implicated two thousand men; Shining impeached him for the false charge.

sentences.zh: 已，聰情得抵罪，帝乃益信世寧。

translations.literal: Before long Cong's circumstances warranted punishment; the emperor then trusted Shining all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Cong's guilt was established and he was punished; the emperor then trusted Shining all the more.

sentences.zh: 王瓊修郤陳九疇，將致之死。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong nursed a grudge against Chen Jiuchou and was about to bring about his death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong, nursing a grudge against Chen Jiuchou, was about to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 以世寧救，得戍。

translations.literal: Through Shining's rescue, he was banished to frontier garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to Shining's intervention, he was sentenced to frontier garrison duty instead.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王時中罷，以世寧代，加太子太保。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Shizhong was dismissed; Shining replaced him, with addition of Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of war Wang Shizhong was dismissed; Shining replaced him and was made senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 再辭不得命，乃陳兵政十事，曰定武略、崇憲職、重將權、增武備、更賞罰、馭土夷、足邊備、絕弊源、正謬誤、惜人才。

translations.literal: Twice declining he could not obtain permission; he then presented ten matters on military administration: fixing martial strategy, honoring censorial duties, weighting generals' authority, increasing armaments, reforming rewards and punishments, controlling native tribes, sufficing border preparations, cutting off sources of abuse, correcting errors, and cherishing talent.
translations.idiomatic: After twice declining without success, he presented ten proposals on military administration: fix martial strategy, honor censorial duties, strengthen generals' authority, increase armaments, reform rewards and punishments, control native tribes, strengthen border defenses, cut off sources of abuse, correct errors, and cherish talent.

sentences.zh: 所言多破常格，帝優旨答之。

translations.literal: What he said mostly broke conventional patterns; the emperor answered with gracious edict.
translations.idiomatic: Most of his proposals broke with convention; the emperor responded with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 土魯番貢使乞歸哈密城，易降人牙木蘭。

translations.literal: Turpan tribute envoys asked to recover Hami city in exchange for the surrendered man Yabulum.
translations.idiomatic: Turpan tribute envoys asked to recover the city of Hami in exchange for the surrendered man Yabulum.

sentences.zh: 王瓊上其事。

translations.literal: Wang Qiong memorialized on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qiong memorialized on the matter.

sentences.zh: 世寧言：「先朝不惜棄大寧、交阯，何有於哈密。

translations.literal: Shining said: "The previous dynasty did not hesitate to abandon Daning and Jiaozhi—what is there in Hami?
translations.idiomatic: Shining said, "The previous dynasty did not hesitate to abandon Daning and Jiaozhi—what is Hami by comparison?

sentences.zh: 況初封忠順為我外藩，而自罕慎以來三為土魯番所執，遂狎與戎比，以疲我中國，耗財老師，戎得挾以邀索。

translations.literal: Moreover when Zhongshun was first enfeoffed as our outer dependency, since Han Shen it has thrice been seized by Turpan, then grown familiar and allied with the barbarians, to weary our China, drain wealth and age the army, and let the barbarians use it to extort.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, when Zhongshun was first enfeoffed as our outer dependency, since Han Shen it has been seized by Turpan three times and has grown familiar with the barbarians, wearing down China, draining the treasury, and aging the army while the barbarians use Hami to extort concessions.

sentences.zh: 臣以為此與國初所封元孽和順、寧順、安定三王等耳。

translations.literal: Your subject thinks this is the same as the three kings Heshun, Ningshun, and Anding, Yuan remnant lines enfeoffed at the dynasty's founding.
translations.idiomatic: In my view this is no different from the three kings Heshun, Ningshun, and Anding—Yuan remnant lines enfeoffed at the dynasty's founding.

sentences.zh: 安定在哈密內，近甘肅，今存亡不可知。

translations.literal: Anding was within Hami, near Gansu; now whether he exists or not cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Anding was within Hami, near Gansu; whether his line still exists is unknown.

sentences.zh: 我一切不問，獨重哈密何也？

translations.literal: We ask nothing of all that—why single out Hami for weight?
translations.idiomatic: We pay no attention to any of that—why single out Hami for special concern?

sentences.zh: 宜專守河西，謝絕哈密。

translations.literal: We ought to concentrate on holding Hexi and decline Hami.
translations.idiomatic: We ought to concentrate on holding Hexi and cut ties with Hami.

sentences.zh: 牙木蘭本曲先衛人，反正歸順，非納降比，彼安得索之？

translations.literal: Yabulum was originally a man of Quxian Guard who turned from wrong and submitted in loyalty—not comparable to those who surrendered in defeat; how can they demand him?
translations.idiomatic: Yabulum was originally from Quxian Guard and turned from rebellion to loyal submission—not comparable to ordinary defectors; how can they demand him back?

sentences.zh: 唐悉怛謀事可鑒也。

translations.literal: The affair of Tang's Sidanmo can serve as a mirror.
translations.idiomatic: The affair of Sidanmo in Tang times should serve as a warning.

sentences.zh: 」張璁等皆主瓊議，格不用，獨留牙木蘭不遣。

translations.literal: " Zhang Cong and others all upheld Qiong's view; it was blocked and not used; only Yabulum was retained and not sent away.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Cong and others all supported Qiong's view; the proposal was rejected, but Yabulum alone was retained and not sent back.

sentences.zh: 居兵部三月求去，帝不許，免朝參。

translations.literal: After three months in the Ministry of War he asked to leave; the emperor did not permit it but exempted him from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: After three months as minister of war he asked to resign; the emperor refused but exempted him from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 世寧又上備邊三事。

translations.literal: Shining again presented three matters on border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Shining again submitted three proposals on border defense.

sentences.zh: 固稱疾篤，乃聽乘傳歸，給廩隸如制。

translations.literal: He firmly claimed grave illness; only then was he allowed to return by relay post, with grain allowance and attendants as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly claimed grave illness; only then was he permitted to return by relay post, with grain allowance and attendants as regulations provided.

sentences.zh: 歸數月，復起南京兵部尚書，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Several months after returning he was again raised as Minister of War at Nanjing; he firmly declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Several months after returning home he was again appointed minister of war at Nanjing; he firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 九年秋卒。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the autumn of year 9.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚端敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and granted the title Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian and granted the title Duanmin (Upright and Keen).

sentences.zh: 世寧風格峻整，居官廉。

translations.literal: Shining's manner was stern and ordered; in office he was incorrupt.
translations.idiomatic: Shining's manner was stern and dignified, and he was incorrupt in office.

sentences.zh: 疾惡若仇，而薦達賢士如不及。

translations.literal: He hated evil as if it were a personal enemy, yet recommended and advanced worthy men as if he could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: He hated evil as a personal enemy, yet recommended worthy men as if he could not do so fast enough.

sentences.zh: 都御史馬昊、陳九疇坐累廢；

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Ma Hao and Chen Jiuchou were implicated and dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: Censors-in-chief Ma Hao and Chen Jiuchou were implicated and dismissed;

sentences.zh: 副使施儒、楊必進考察被黜；

translations.literal: Vice Commissioners Shi Ru and Yang Bijin were dismissed in merit review;
translations.idiomatic: vice commissioners Shi Ru and Yang Bijin were dismissed in merit review;

sentences.zh: 御史李潤、副使範輅為時所抑，連章薦之。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Li Run and Vice Commissioner Fan Lu were suppressed by the times—he memorialized in succession recommending them.
translations.idiomatic: investigating censor Li Run and vice commissioner Fan Lu were suppressed by their contemporaries—he memorialized repeatedly recommending them.

sentences.zh: 與人語，吶不出口。

translations.literal: Speaking with others, he stammered and words would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation he stammered and could barely speak.

sentences.zh: 及具疏，援據古今，洞中窾會。

translations.literal: When he prepared memorials, citing ancient and modern, he penetrated to the vital point.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when he drafted memorials, citing ancient and modern precedents, he struck straight to the heart of the matter.

sentences.zh: 與李承勛善，而持議不茍合。

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Li Chengxun, yet held to his views without careless agreement.
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Li Chengxun, yet refused to compromise his views carelessly.

sentences.zh: 承勛欲授隴勝官，復芒部故地，世寧言勝非隴氏子，芒氏不當復立。

translations.literal: Chengxun wished to grant Long Sheng office and restore Mang territory; Shining said Sheng was not a son of the Long clan and the Mang line ought not be re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun wished to grant Long Sheng office and restore the Mang territory; Shining argued that Sheng was not a son of the Long clan and the Mang line ought not be re-established.

sentences.zh: 始以議禮與張璁、桂萼合，璁、萼德之，欲援以自助。

translations.literal: At first on the Rites debate he agreed with Zhang Cong and Gui E; Cong and E were grateful and wished to draw him in to help themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At first he sided with Zhang Cong and Gui E on the Rites debate; they were grateful and wished to draw him in as an ally.

sentences.zh: 世寧不肯附會，論事多牴牾。

translations.literal: Shining would not join in collusion; on affairs his views often clashed.
translations.idiomatic: Shining refused to collude, and his views often clashed with theirs.

sentences.zh: 萼議欲銷兵，世寧力折之。

translations.literal: Gui E proposed wishing to reduce the army; Shining strongly refuted it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui E proposed reducing the army, Shining strongly refuted him.

sentences.zh: 昌化伯以他姓子冒封，下廷議。

translations.literal: The Earl of Changhua used another surname's son to usurp enfeoffment; the matter was sent down for court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Changhua had a son of another surname fraudulently enfeoffed; the matter was referred to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 世寧言：「吾輩不得以厚賂故，誣朝廷」，萼為色變。

translations.literal: Shining said: "We must not, because of heavy bribes, deceive the court"; E's countenance changed.
translations.idiomatic: Shining said, "We must not deceive the court because of heavy bribes"; Gui E turned pale.

sentences.zh: 萼方為吏部，而世寧引疾，言：「天變人窮，盜賊滋起，咎在吏、戶、兵三部不得人。

translations.literal: E was just Minister of Personnel while Shining cited illness, saying: "Heaven's changes and men's extremity—bandits rise in number; the blame lies in the ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and War not having the right men.
translations.idiomatic: Gui E had just become minister of personnel when Shining cited illness, saying, "Heaven shows omens and the people are desperate; bandits multiply—the blame lies with the ministries of Personnel, Revenue, and War for lacking the right men.

sentences.zh: 兵部尤重，請避賢路。

translations.literal: The Ministry of War is especially weighty; I ask to yield the path to the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of War is especially important; I ask to yield the post to someone more worthy.

sentences.zh: 」又以哈密議，語侵璁，諸大臣皆忌之。

translations.literal: " Also because of the Hami debate, his words offended Cong; the great ministers all envied him.
translations.idiomatic: " He also offended Zhang Cong in the Hami debate, and the senior ministers all resented him.

sentences.zh: 帝始終優禮不替。

translations.literal: The emperor from beginning to end treated him with favor without change.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nonetheless treated him with unwavering favor throughout.

sentences.zh: 子純、繼。

translations.literal: Sons Chun and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Chun and Ji.

sentences.zh: 純以父任知肇慶府，有才行。

translations.literal: Chun, through his father's privilege, became prefect of Zhaoqing; he had ability and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Chun, through his father's privilege, became prefect of Zhaoqing and showed both ability and integrity.

sentences.zh: 繼幼不慧，不為世寧知。

translations.literal: Ji in youth was not clever and was not known to Shining.
translations.idiomatic: Ji seemed dull in youth and was unknown to his father.

sentences.zh: 世寧在江西出討賊，部將入見繼。

translations.literal: When Shining in Jiangxi went out to campaign against bandits, a deputy general came to see Ji.
translations.idiomatic: While Shining was in Jiangxi campaigning against bandits, a deputy general came to visit Ji.

sentences.zh: 繼為指陣法，進退離合甚詳，凡三日。

translations.literal: Ji explained battle formations for him, advance and retreat, dispersal and concentration in great detail, for three days in all.
translations.idiomatic: Ji explained battle formations to him in great detail—advance, retreat, dispersal, and concentration—for three full days.

sentences.zh: 世寧歸閱，大異之。

translations.literal: When Shining returned and reviewed it, he was greatly astonished.
translations.idiomatic: When Shining returned and read the notes, he was astonished.

sentences.zh: 知其故，嘆曰：「吾有子不自識，何也？

translations.literal: Learning the reason, he sighed: "I have a son I did not know—how can this be?
translations.idiomatic: Learning what had happened, he sighed, "I had a son I did not know—how could that be?

sentences.zh: 」自是擊賊，輒令繼從，與策方略。

translations.literal: " From then on whenever he struck bandits he always had Ji follow and plan strategy with him.
translations.idiomatic: " From then on, whenever he campaigned against bandits, he had Ji accompany him and help plan strategy.

sentences.zh: 世寧十不失三，繼十不失一。

translations.literal: Shining was right seven times in ten; Ji was right nine times in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Shining was right seven times in ten; Ji was right nine times in ten.

sentences.zh: 世寧方草疏論宸濠，繼請曰：「是且重得禍。

translations.literal: Shining was just drafting a memorial on Chenhao; Ji begged: "This will again bring heavy disaster.
translations.idiomatic: As Shining was drafting a memorial denouncing Chenhao, Ji pleaded, "This will bring disaster upon you again.

sentences.zh: 」世寧曰：「吾已許國，遑恤其他。

translations.literal: " Shining said: "I have already pledged myself to the state—how can I spare thought for other things?
translations.idiomatic: " Shining said, "I have already pledged myself to the state—how can I spare thought for anything else?

sentences.zh: 」及世寧下獄，繼念其父，病死。

translations.literal: " When Shining entered prison, Ji thinking of his father died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: " When Shining was imprisoned, Ji, grieving for his father, died of illness.

sentences.zh: 李承勛，字立卿，嘉魚人。

translations.literal: Li Chengxun, styled Liqing, was a man of Jiayu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chengxun, styled Liqing, was a native of Jiayu.

sentences.zh: 父田，進士，官右副都御史，巡撫順天。

translations.literal: His father Tian was a jinshi, served as Right Vice Censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tian was a jinshi who served as right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 有操執，為政不苛。

translations.literal: He had integrity in conduct; in administration he was not harsh.
translations.idiomatic: He was a man of integrity who governed without harshness.

sentences.zh: 承勛舉弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: Chengxun passed the jinshi in the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun passed the jinshi in Hongzhi year 6.

sentences.zh: 由太湖知縣遷南京刑部主事。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Taihu he was transferred to director in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from magistrate of Taihu to a directorship in the Nanjing Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 歷工部郎中，遷南昌知府。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of Works, then was transferred to prefect of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Works, then was appointed prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 正德六年，贛州賊犯新淦，執參政趙士賢。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhengde, Ganzhou bandits attacked Xingan and seized Vice Commissioner Zhao Shixian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde year 6, Ganzhou bandits attacked Xingan and seized Vice Commissioner Zhao Shixian.

sentences.zh: 靖安賊據越王嶺瑪瑙岸，華林賊又陷瑞州。

translations.literal: Jing'an bandits held Yuewang Ridge and Manao Bank; Hualin bandits also took Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'an bandits held Yuewang Ridge and Manao Bank, while Hualin bandits also captured Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 諸道兵不敢前。

translations.literal: Troops from the various circuits dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops from the various circuits dared not advance.

sentences.zh: 承勛督民兵剿，數有功。

translations.literal: Chengxun supervised militia in suppression and several times had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun led militia in suppression campaigns and won several victories.

sentences.zh: 華林賊殺副使周憲，憲軍大潰。

translations.literal: Hualin bandits killed Vice Commissioner Zhou Xian; Xian's army collapsed in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Hualin bandits killed Vice Commissioner Zhou Xian, and Zhou's army collapsed in rout.

sentences.zh: 承勛單騎入憲營，眾乃復集。

translations.literal: Chengxun alone on horseback entered Xian's camp; the troops then gathered again.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun rode alone into Zhou's camp and rallied the scattered troops.

sentences.zh: 都御史陳金即檄承勛討之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-chief Chen Jin immediately dispatched Chengxun to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Chen Jin immediately ordered Chengxun to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 賊黨王奇聽撫，搜得其衷刃，縱使還。

translations.literal: The bandit partisan Wang Qi heard pacification offered; searching found a dagger hidden in his robe; he was released to return.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Wang Qi accepted an offer of pacification; a search found a hidden dagger, yet Chengxun released him to return.

sentences.zh: 奇感泣，誓以死報。

translations.literal: Qi wept in gratitude and vowed to repay with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Qi wept with gratitude and vowed to repay Chengxun with his life.

sentences.zh: 承勛令奇密入寨，說降其黨為內應，而親率所部登山。

translations.literal: Chengxun ordered Qi secretly to enter the stockade and persuade his partisans to surrender as inner collaborators, while he personally led his troops up the mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun sent Qi secretly into the stockade to persuade his comrades to serve as inside collaborators, while he personally led his troops up the mountain.

sentences.zh: 奇夜拔柵，官軍奮而前，降者自內出，賊遂潰。

translations.literal: Qi by night pulled up the palisade; government troops charged forward; those who surrendered came out from within; the bandits then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Qi pulled up the palisade by night; government troops charged forward as the defectors emerged from within, and the bandits collapsed.

sentences.zh: 已，從金斬賊渠羅光權、胡雪二，華林賊平。

translations.literal: Before long, following Jin, he beheaded bandit chiefs Luo Guangquan and Hu Xue; Hualin bandits were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, following Jin, he beheaded the bandit chiefs Luo Guangquan and Hu Xue, and the Hualin bandits were pacified.

sentences.zh: 鎮守中貴黎安誣承勛擅易賊首王浩八獄詞，坐下吏。

translations.literal: Garrison eunuch Li An falsely charged Chengxun with arbitrarily altering the prison testimony of bandit chief Wang Haoba; he was sent down to the officials.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison eunuch Li An falsely accused Chengxun of arbitrarily altering bandit chief Wang Haoba's testimony, and Chengxun was handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 大理卿燕忠即訊，得白。

translations.literal: Chief justice Yan Zhong immediately examined the case and cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: Chief justice Yan Zhong examined the case immediately and cleared him.

sentences.zh: 舉治行卓異，超遷浙工按察使。

translations.literal: Recommended for outstanding conduct in office, he was specially promoted to Surveillance Commissioner of Zhejiang and Works.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended for outstanding conduct in office, he was specially promoted to surveillance commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 歷陜西、河南左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shaanxi and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as left and right provincial administration commissioner of Shaanxi and Henan.

sentences.zh: 以右副都御史巡撫遼東。

translations.literal: As Right Vice Censor-in-chief he was grand coordinator of Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: As right vice censor-in-chief he was appointed grand coordinator of Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 邊備久弛，開原尤甚。

translations.literal: Border preparations had long been lax; Kaiyuan especially so.
translations.idiomatic: Border defenses had long been neglected, especially at Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 士馬才十二，墻堡墩臺圮殆盡。

translations.literal: Soldiers and horses numbered only twelve thousand; walls, forts, beacon towers were nearly all ruined.
translations.idiomatic: There were only twelve thousand soldiers and horses, and walls, forts, and beacon towers were nearly all in ruins.

sentences.zh: 將士依城塹自守，城外數百里悉為諸部射獵地，承勛疏請修築。

translations.literal: Officers and soldiers relied on the moat within the city for defense; several hundred li outside were all hunting grounds for the various tribes; Chengxun memorialized asking to repair and build.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and soldiers defended only within the city moat, while for hundreds of li beyond the walls the various tribes used the land as hunting grounds; Chengxun memorialized asking to repair and build defenses.

sentences.zh: 會世宗立，發帑銀四十余萬兩。

translations.literal: When Shizong succeeded, treasury silver of more than four hundred thousand taels was issued.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, more than four hundred thousand taels of silver were issued from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 承勛命步將四人各一軍守要害，身負畚鍤先士卒。

translations.literal: Chengxun ordered four infantry generals each with one army to guard key points; he himself carried basket and spade ahead of the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun assigned four infantry generals, each with an army, to guard key points, and himself carried tools ahead of the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 凡為城塹各九萬一千四百余丈，墩堡百八十有一。

translations.literal: In all they made moats totaling ninety-one thousand four hundred-plus zhang each, and one hundred eighty-one beacon forts.
translations.idiomatic: In all they built moats totaling more than ninety-one thousand four hundred zhang and one hundred eighty-one beacon forts.

sentences.zh: 招逋逃三千二百人，開屯田千五百頃。

translations.literal: They recruited three thousand two hundred fugitives and opened fifteen hundred qing of garrison fields.
translations.idiomatic: They recruited three thousand two hundred fugitives and opened fifteen hundred qing of garrison farmland.

sentences.zh: 又城中固、鐵嶺；

translations.literal: They also walled Gu and Tieling within the cities;
translations.idiomatic: They also fortified Gu and Tieling;

sentences.zh: 斷陰山、遼河之交；

translations.literal: cut the junction of Yin Mountain and the Liao River;
translations.idiomatic: blocked the junction of Yin Mountain and the Liao River;

sentences.zh: 城蒲河、撫順，扼要沖。

translations.literal: walled Pu River and Fushun, holding strategic passes.
translations.idiomatic: and walled Pu River and Fushun, seizing strategic passes.

sentences.zh: 邊防甚固。
