translations.literal: Border defense was very solid.
translations.idiomatic: Border defenses became very secure.

sentences.zh: 錄功，進秩一等。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; his rank was advanced one grade.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded and his rank was advanced one grade.

sentences.zh: 又數陳軍民利病，鹹報可。

translations.literal: He also repeatedly presented benefits and harms to army and people; all received approval.
translations.idiomatic: He also repeatedly presented proposals on matters affecting army and people, and all were approved.

sentences.zh: 以疾歸。

translations.literal: Because of illness he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home due to illness.

sentences.zh: 起故官，蒞南院。

translations.literal: He was raised to his former office and took charge of the Southern Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to his former post and took charge of the Southern Censorate.

sentences.zh: 三遷刑部尚書，加太子少保。

translations.literal: Three times transferred, he became Minister of Justice, with addition of Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: After three promotions he became minister of justice and was made junior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 帝以京營多弊，欲振飭之。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the capital camps had many abuses, wished to revive and rectify them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, finding many abuses in the capital camps, wished to reform them.

sentences.zh: 遂加承勛太子太保，改兵部尚書兼左都御史，專督團營。

translations.literal: Thereupon Chengxun was made Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, changed to Minister of War concurrently Left Censor-in-chief, exclusively supervising the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun was made senior guardian of the heir apparent, transferred to minister of war concurrently with left censor-in-chief, and placed exclusively in charge of the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 尋兼掌都察院。

translations.literal: Soon he also concurrently directed the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also took charge of the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 以疾，三疏乞休，且言：「山西潞城賊以四道兵討之，不統於一人，故無功。

translations.literal: Because of illness, thrice memorializing he begged retirement, and moreover said: "Shanxi Lucheng bandits—with four-circuit troops campaigning against them, not unified under one man, therefore no achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Citing illness, he thrice memorialized begging retirement and said, "The Lucheng bandits of Shanxi were attacked by troops from four circuits without unified command, and therefore achieved nothing.

sentences.zh: 川、貴芒部之役措置乖方，再勝再叛，宜命伍文定深計，毋專用兵。

translations.literal: The Sichuan-Guizhou Mang campaign was arranged perversely; twice victorious, twice rebelled—Wu Wending should be ordered to plan deeply and not rely solely on arms.
translations.idiomatic: The Mang campaign in Sichuan and Guizhou was mishandled, with victories followed by renewed rebellion; Wu Wending should be ordered to plan carefully and not rely solely on military force.

sentences.zh: 豐、沛河工，二年三易大臣，工不就，宜令知水利者各陳所見，而俾侍郎潘希曾度可否。

translations.literal: Feng and Pei river works—in two years three changes of great ministers, the work not completed—those who understand water control should each present their views, and Vice Minister Pan Xizeng judge feasibility.
translations.idiomatic: For the river works at Feng and Pei, three ministers were replaced in two years without completing the work; experts in water control should each present their views, and Vice Minister Pan Xizeng should assess feasibility.

sentences.zh: 其尤要者，在決壅蔽患。

translations.literal: What is especially vital lies in resolving the harm of obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Most vital of all is to resolve the harm of obstruction and concealment.

sentences.zh: 仿唐、宋轉對、次對故事，不時召見大臣。

translations.literal: Following Tang and Song precedents of rotating responses and second responses, summon great ministers from time to time.
translations.idiomatic: Following Tang and Song precedents of rotating and second responses, the court should summon senior ministers from time to time.

sentences.zh: 」帝不允辭，下其議於所司。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not permit his resignation and sent his proposals down to the relevant offices.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused his resignation and referred his proposals to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 時秦、晉、楚、蜀歲祲，詔免田賦。

translations.literal: At the time Qin, Jin, Chu, and Shu suffered annual famine; an edict exempted land tax.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Qin, Jin, Chu, and Shu suffered crop failure; an edict exempted land tax.

sentences.zh: 承勛言：「有司例十月始征賦。

translations.literal: Chengxun said: "Offices by rule begin collecting tax in the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun said, "By rule local offices begin collecting tax in the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 今九月矣，恐官吏督趣，陰圖乾沒。

translations.literal: Now it is already the ninth month; I fear officials will press collection and secretly plot embezzlement.
translations.idiomatic: It is already the ninth month, and I fear officials will press for collection and secretly embezzle the funds.

sentences.zh: 宜及其未征，遣官馳告以所蠲數。

translations.literal: Before collection begins, officials should be dispatched post-haste to announce the exempted amounts.
translations.idiomatic: Before collection begins, officials should be dispatched post-haste to announce the exempted amounts.

sentences.zh: 山陬僻壤，俾悉戶曉。

translations.literal: In mountain recesses and remote places, let every household be informed.
translations.idiomatic: In mountain recesses and remote districts, every household should be informed.

sentences.zh: 有司不能奉宣德意者，罪之。

translations.literal: Officials who cannot carry out the imperial intent should be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Officials who fail to carry out the imperial intent should be punished.

sentences.zh: 撫按失舉奏，並坐。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and regional inspectors who fail to memorialize should be punished jointly.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinators and regional inspectors who fail to report violations should be punished as well.

sentences.zh: 」帝褒納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 奏奪京營把總湯清職。

translations.literal: He memorialized to strip Tang Qing, company commander of the capital camps, of his post.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to strip Tang Qing, a company commander of the capital camps, of his post.

sentences.zh: 郭勛為求復，語侵承勛。

translations.literal: Guo Xun pleaded for his restoration, his words offending Chengxun.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Xun pleaded for his restoration, his words offending Chengxun.

sentences.zh: 承勛因求退，給事中王準等劾勛恣。

translations.literal: Chengxun thereupon asked to retire; supervising secretaries Wang Zhun and others impeached Xun for arrogance.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun thereupon asked to retire; supervising secretaries Wang Zhun and others impeached Guo Xun for arrogance.

sentences.zh: 乃敕責勛，而下清法司。

translations.literal: The emperor then rebuked Xun by edict and sent Qing down to the judicial offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then rebuked Guo Xun by edict and referred Qing to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書胡世寧致仕，詔承勛還部代之。

translations.literal: Minister of War Hu Shining retired; an edict ordered Chengxun back to the ministry to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of war Hu Shining retired; an edict ordered Chengxun back to the ministry to replace him.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「朝廷有大政及推舉文武大臣，必下廷議。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "When the court has great policies or recommends civil and military great ministers, the matter must go to court deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "When the court has major policies or recommends senior civil and military officials, the matter must be referred to court deliberation.

sentences.zh: 議者率相顧不發，拱手聽。

translations.literal: Deliberators generally look at one another and do not speak, folding hands to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberators generally look at one another in silence, folding their hands and waiting to be told what to do.

sentences.zh: 宜及未議前，備條所議，布告與議者，俾先諗其故，然後平心商質，各盡所懷。

translations.literal: Before deliberation, the matters should be fully itemized and announced to participants so they may first understand the reasons, then discuss calmly and each express their views fully.
translations.idiomatic: Before deliberation begins, the issues should be fully itemized and circulated to participants so they understand the background, then discuss calmly and each state their views fully.

sentences.zh: 議茍不合，聽其別奏。

translations.literal: If deliberation does not agree, they should be allowed to submit separate memorials.
translations.idiomatic: If deliberation fails to reach agreement, participants should be allowed to submit separate memorials.

sentences.zh: 庶足盡諸臣之見，而所議者公。

translations.literal: Thus the views of all ministers may be fully expressed and what is deliberated will be fair.
translations.idiomatic: Thus all ministers' views may be fully heard and deliberation will be fair.

sentences.zh: 」帝然其言，下詔申飭。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his words and issued an edict to enforce it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor approved his proposal and issued an edict reinforcing it.

sentences.zh: 尋命兼督團營。

translations.literal: Soon he was also ordered to supervise the regiment camps concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also ordered to supervise the regiment camps concurrently.

sentences.zh: 言官攻張璁、桂萼黨，並及承勛。

translations.literal: Censorial officials attacked the faction of Zhang Cong and Gui E, implicating Chengxun as well.
translations.idiomatic: Censorial officials attacked the faction of Zhang Cong and Gui E and implicated Chengxun as well.

sentences.zh: 承勛連章求退，帝復溫旨答之。

translations.literal: Chengxun memorialized repeatedly asking to retire; the emperor again answered with a warm edict.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun memorialized repeatedly asking to retire; the emperor again responded with a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 中官出鎮者，率暴橫。

translations.literal: Eunuchs sent out to garrison posts were generally violent and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs assigned to garrison posts were generally violent and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 承勛因諫官李鳳毛等言，先後裁二十七人，又革錦衣官五百人，監局冒役數千人。

translations.literal: On the advice of remonstrating officials Li Fengmao and others, Chengxun dismissed twenty-seven in succession, removed five hundred Embroidered Uniform Guard posts, and cut thousands of false registrations in supervisory offices.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on remonstrating officials Li Fengmao and others, Chengxun dismissed twenty-seven eunuchs in succession, cut five hundred Embroidered Uniform Guard posts, and eliminated thousands of fraudulent registrations in supervisory offices.

sentences.zh: 獨禦馬監未汰，復因給事中田秋奏，多所裁減。

translations.literal: Only the Imperial Horse Stud was not yet reduced; again on supervising secretary Tian Qiu's memorial, many cuts were made.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Imperial Horse Stud had not yet been reduced; again, on supervising secretary Tian Qiu's memorial, many further cuts were made.

sentences.zh: 而請以騰驤四衛屬部，核詭冒，制可。

translations.literal: He also requested placing the four Tengxiang guards under the ministry and auditing fraudulent registrations—approved.
translations.idiomatic: He also requested placing the four Tengxiang guards under the ministry and auditing fraudulent registrations; the proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 中官言曩彰義門破也先，東市剿曹賊，皆四衛功，以直內故易集，隸兵部不便。

translations.literal: Eunuchs said that formerly at Zhangyi Gate they broke Esen, and at East Market they suppressed Cao's bandits—all achievements of the four guards; because they were directly inside they assembled easily; subordination to the Ministry of War was inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs argued that at Zhangyi Gate they had defeated Esen and at East Market they had suppressed Cao's rebels—all feats of the four guards; because they were directly under the palace they could be assembled quickly, and subordination to the Ministry of War would be inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 承勛言：「彰義門之戰，禍由王振。

translations.literal: Chengxun said: "The battle at Zhangyi Gate—the disaster came from Wang Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun said, "At the battle of Zhangyi Gate the disaster came from Wang Zhen.

sentences.zh: 東市作賊，即曹吉祥也。

translations.literal: The rebel at East Market was none other than Cao Xiangji.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel at East Market was none other than Cao Xiangji.

sentences.zh: 」帝卒從承勛議，歸兵部。

translations.literal: " The emperor ultimately followed Chengxun's view and returned them to the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor ultimately followed Chengxun's view and returned the guards to the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 寇犯大同，議遣大臣督兵。

translations.literal: Bandits invaded Datong; it was proposed to send a great minister to supervise troops.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders invaded Datong, and the court proposed sending a senior minister to supervise the troops.

sentences.zh: 眾推都御史王憲，憲不肯行。

translations.literal: All recommended Censor-in-chief Wang Xian; Xian refused to go.
translations.idiomatic: All recommended censor-in-chief Wang Xian, but Wang refused to go.

sentences.zh: 給事中夏言謂承勛曰：「事急，公當請行。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xia Yan said to Chengxun: "The matter is urgent—you should request to go.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xia Yan told Chengxun, "The matter is urgent—you should volunteer to go.

sentences.zh: 」承勛竟不請。

translations.literal: " Chengxun ultimately did not request it.
translations.idiomatic: " Chengxun ultimately did not volunteer.

sentences.zh: 給事中趙廷瑞並劾之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries Zhao Tingrui and others impeached both.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries Zhao Tingrui and others impeached both men.

sentences.zh: 會寇退，罷。

translations.literal: When the bandits withdrew, the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew, the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十年春，大風晝晦，帝憂邊事。

translations.literal: In the spring of the tenth year, great wind darkened the day; the emperor worried over border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of year 10 a great wind darkened the sky by day, and the emperor grew anxious about border affairs.

sentences.zh: 承勛言：「去歲冰合，敵騎盡入河套。

translations.literal: Chengxun said: "Last year the rivers froze over and enemy horsemen all entered the Ordos.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun said, "Last year the rivers froze and enemy horsemen poured into the Ordos.

sentences.zh: 延、寧、固原皆當警備。

translations.literal: Yan, Ning, and Guyuan all should be on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Ning, and Guyuan should all be placed on alert.

sentences.zh: 甘肅軍餉專仰河東，宜於蘭州糴貯，以備緩急。

translations.literal: Gansu's military provisions rely solely on Hedong; grain should be purchased and stored at Lanzhou for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Gansu's military provisions depend entirely on Hedong; grain should be purchased and stored at Lanzhou against emergencies.

sentences.zh: 曩河西患土魯番，今亦卜喇又深入。

translations.literal: Formerly Hexi suffered from Turpan; now Yibula has again penetrated deep.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Hexi suffered from Turpan; now Yibula has again penetrated deep into the region.

sentences.zh: 兩寇雲擾，孤危益甚。

translations.literal: Two enemies swarm like clouds; isolation and peril grow worse.
translations.idiomatic: With two enemies swarming like clouds, the frontier grows ever more isolated and perilous.

sentences.zh: 套寇出入，並經莊浪。

translations.literal: Ordos bandits come and go, all passing through Zhuanglang.
translations.idiomatic: Ordos raiders come and go, all passing through Zhuanglang.

sentences.zh: 急宜繕塞設險，斷臂截踵，使不得相合。

translations.literal: We must urgently repair defenses and set barriers—sever arm and cut heel—so they cannot join.
translations.idiomatic: We must urgently repair defenses and establish barriers—cut the arm and sever the heel—so the two enemies cannot join forces.

sentences.zh: 兀良哈最近京師，不善撫，即門庭寇。

translations.literal: Uriankhai are nearest the capital; poorly pacified, they become bandits at the doorstep.
translations.idiomatic: The Uriankhai are closest to the capital; if poorly pacified, they become raiders at the doorstep.

sentences.zh: 雲南安鳳之叛，軍民困敝，臨安、蒙自盜賊復興，曠日淹時，恐釀大患。

translations.literal: In Yunnan An Feng's rebellion has exhausted troops and people; bandits have risen again at Lin'an and Mengzi; prolonged delay may brew great disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Yunnan, An Feng's rebellion has exhausted troops and civilians, bandits have risen again at Lin'an and Mengzi, and prolonged delay may brew a greater disaster.

sentences.zh: 交阯世子流寓老撾，異日歸命請援，或據地求封，皆未可測。

translations.literal: The Jiaozhi heir-apparent wanders in Laos; someday he may return and plea for aid, or seize land and seek enfeoffment—all unforeseeable.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiaozhi heir-apparent wanders in Laos; someday he may return to submit and request aid, or seize territory and seek enfeoffment—all unforeseeable.

sentences.zh: 惟急用人理財，俾邊鄙無虞。

translations.literal: Only urgently employ men and manage finances, so the frontiers may be without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Only by urgently appointing capable men and managing finances can the frontiers be kept secure.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納焉。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 承勛瀋毅有大略。

translations.literal: Chengxun was grave and resolute, with great strategic vision.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun was grave and resolute, with great strategic vision.

sentences.zh: 帝所信任，自輔臣外，獨承勛與胡世寧，大事輒咨訪。

translations.literal: Of those the emperor trusted, apart from chief ministers only Chengxun and Hu Shining—on great matters he would consult them.
translations.idiomatic: Among those the emperor trusted, apart from chief ministers only Chengxun and Hu Shining were consulted on major affairs.

sentences.zh: 二人亦孜孜奉國，知無不言。

translations.literal: The two also served the state diligently, speaking whatever they knew.
translations.idiomatic: The two also served the state diligently and spoke frankly on every matter they knew.

sentences.zh: 世寧卒半歲，承勛亦卒，帝深嗟悼。

translations.literal: Half a year after Shining died Chengxun also died; the emperor deeply mourned.
translations.idiomatic: Half a year after Shining died, Chengxun also died, and the emperor deeply mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚康惠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian and granted the title Kanghui.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian and granted the title Kanghui (Peaceful and Kind).

sentences.zh: 所賚予，常典外，特賜白金、彩幣、米蔬諸物。

translations.literal: What was bestowed, beyond regular rites, specially included white gold, colored silks, grain, vegetables, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the usual rites, he was specially granted white gold, colored silks, grain, vegetables, and other goods.

sentences.zh: 承勛官四十年，家無余資。

translations.literal: Chengxun served forty years in office; his family had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Chengxun served forty years in office, yet his family had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 其議「大禮」，亦與世寧相合雲。

translations.literal: His views on the "Great Rites" also accorded with Shining's, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: It is said that his views on the Great Rites also accorded with Shining's.

sentences.zh: 三邊總督曾銑議復河套，大學士夏言主之。

translations.literal: Three-frontier Grand Coordinator Zeng Xian proposed recovering the Ordos; Grand Secretary Xia Yan supported it.
translations.idiomatic: Three-frontier grand coordinator Zeng Xian proposed recovering the Ordos, and grand secretary Xia Yan supported him.

sentences.zh: 數下優旨獎銑，令以旂集廷臣議。

translations.literal: Several times favorable edicts praised Xian and ordered Yiqi to gather court ministers for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor several times issued favorable edicts praising Zeng Xian and ordered Yiqi to gather court ministers for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 以旂等力主銑議。

translations.literal: Yiqi and others strongly upheld Xian's proposal.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi and others strongly upheld Zeng Xian's proposal.

sentences.zh: 議上，帝意忽變，嚴旨咎銑，令再議。

translations.literal: When deliberation was submitted, the emperor's intent suddenly changed; a stern edict blamed Xian and ordered re-deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: When the deliberation was submitted, the emperor's intent suddenly changed; a stern edict blamed Zeng Xian and ordered a new deliberation.

sentences.zh: 以旂等惶恐，盡反前說。

translations.literal: Yiqi and others in fear completely reversed their earlier views.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi and others, in fear, completely reversed their earlier position.

sentences.zh: 帝逮銑，令以旂代之。

translations.literal: The emperor arrested Xian and ordered Yiqi to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor arrested Zeng Xian and ordered Yiqi to replace him.

sentences.zh: 套寇自西海還，肆掠永昌，鎮羌總兵官王繼祖禦卻之。

translations.literal: Ordos bandits returning from the Western Sea plundered Yongchang; Regional Commander of Zhenqiang Wang Jizu repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Ordos raiders returning from the Western Sea plundered Yongchang; regional commander of Zhenqiang Wang Jizu repelled them.

sentences.zh: 已，復來犯，並及鎮番、山丹。

translations.literal: Before long they came again, also reaching Zhenfan and Shandan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long they attacked again, reaching Zhenfan and Shandan as well.

sentences.zh: 部將蔡勛、馬宗援三戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Deputies Cai Xun and Ma Zongyuan fought three battles, all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy commanders Cai Xun and Ma Zongyuan fought three battles, all victorious.

sentences.zh: 前後斬首一百四十余級。

translations.literal: In all more than 140 heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In all more than 140 heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 論功，蔭以旂一子。

translations.literal: For merit, one son of Yiqi received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: For merit, one of Yiqi's sons received hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 已而寇數萬復屯寧夏塞外，將大入。

translations.literal: Before long tens of thousands of bandits again camped outside Ningxia's borders, about to invade on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Before long tens of thousands of raiders again camped outside Ningxia's borders, poised for a major invasion.

sentences.zh: 官軍擊之，斬首六十余級，寇宵遁。

translations.literal: Government troops struck them, took more than 60 heads; the bandits fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: Government troops attacked them, took more than 60 heads, and the raiders fled by night.

sentences.zh: 延綏、寧夏開馬市，二鎮市五千匹。

translations.literal: Yansui and Ningxia opened horse markets; the two garrisons traded five thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yansui and Ningxia opened horse markets, and the two garrisons traded five thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 其長狠臺吉等約束所部，終市無嘩。

translations.literal: Their chiefs including Hen Taiji restrained their followers; the market ended without uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Their chiefs, including Hen Taiji, restrained their followers, and the markets concluded without disturbance.

sentences.zh: 以旂以聞。

translations.literal: Yiqi reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Yiqi reported the matter.

sentences.zh: 詔大賚二鎮文武將吏，以旂復賜金幣。

translations.literal: An edict greatly rewarded civil and military officers of the two garrisons; Yiqi was again granted gold and silks.
translations.idiomatic: An edict greatly rewarded the civil and military officers of both garrisons, and Yiqi was again granted gold and silks.

sentences.zh: 錄延綏將士破敵功，再蔭一子。

translations.literal: Recording Yansui officers' and soldiers' merit in defeating the enemy, another son received hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Recording the Yansui officers' and soldiers' merit in defeating the enemy, another of Yiqi's sons received hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 在鎮六年，修延綏城堡四千五百余所，又築蘭州邊垣，加官至太子太保。

translations.literal: Six years in the post, he repaired more than 4,500 castles in Yansui and also built Lanzhou's border wall, raised to Senior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During six years in the post he repaired more than 4,500 fortifications in Yansui and built Lanzhou's border wall, and was promoted to senior guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 比卒，軍民為罷市。

translations.literal: When he died, troops and people closed markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, soldiers and civilians closed their markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚襄敏，再予一子官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian, granted the title Xiangmin, and another son given office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian, granted the title Xiangmin (Assisting and Keen), and another son was given office.

sentences.zh: 范鏓，字平甫，其先江西樂平人，遷瀋陽。

translations.literal: Fan Zong, styled Pingfu; his ancestors were men of Leping in Jiangxi, later moved to Shenyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zong, styled Pingfu, was descended from a family of Leping in Jiangxi that later moved to Shenyang.

sentences.zh: 鏓登正德十二年進士，授工部主事，遷員外郎。

translations.literal: Zong passed the jinshi in the twelfth year of Zhengde, was appointed director in the Ministry of Works, and transferred to vice director.
translations.idiomatic: Zong passed the jinshi in Zhengde year 12, was appointed a director in the Ministry of Works, and was promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖三年，伏闕爭「大禮」，下獄廷杖。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jiajing he prostrated at the palace gate over the "Great Rites," was imprisoned and court-cudgelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing year 3 he prostrated at the palace gate protesting the Great Rites, was imprisoned, and was beaten at court.

sentences.zh: 由戶部郎中改長蘆鹽運司同知，遷河南知府。

translations.literal: From director in the Ministry of Revenue he was changed to vice commissioner of Changlu Salt Transport, then transferred to prefect of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue to vice commissioner of the Changlu Salt Transport Circuit, then was appointed prefect of Henan.

sentences.zh: 歲大饑，巡撫都御史潘塤駁諸請振文牒，候勘實乃發。

translations.literal: In a year of great famine the grand coordinator Pan Kun rejected all petitions for relief documents, waiting for verification before issuing.
translations.idiomatic: During a great famine, grand coordinator Pan Kun rejected all requests for relief documents, insisting on verification before issuing grain.

sentences.zh: 鏓不待報，輒開倉振之，全活十余萬。

translations.literal: Zong without waiting for reply opened granaries and relieved them, saving more than 100,000 lives.
translations.idiomatic: Zong, without waiting for approval, opened the granaries and distributed relief, saving more than 100,000 lives.

sentences.zh: 民爭謳頌鏓，語聞禁中。

translations.literal: The people competed in singing Zong's praise; word reached the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: The people vied in singing Zong's praises, and word reached the palace.

sentences.zh: 帝為責戶部及塤與巡按御史匿災狀。

translations.literal: The emperor rebuked the Ministry of Revenue, Kun, and the touring censor for concealing the disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked the Ministry of Revenue, Pan Kun, and the touring censor for concealing the famine.

sentences.zh: 塤歸罪鏓以自解，被劾罷去，鏓名由此顯。

translations.literal: Kun blamed Zong to extricate himself, was impeached and dismissed; Zong's fame rose thereby.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Kun blamed Zong to save himself, was impeached and dismissed, and Zong's reputation rose accordingly.

sentences.zh: 遷兩淮鹽運使，條上鹺政十要。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Lianghuai Salt Transport Commissioner and presented ten essentials of salt administration.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commissioner of the Lianghuai Salt Transport Circuit and submitted ten essentials for salt administration.

sentences.zh: 歷四川參政，湖廣按察使，浙江、河南左、右布政使。

translations.literal: He served as administration vice commissioner of Sichuan, surveillance commissioner of Huguang, and left and right administration commissioners of Zhejiang and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as administration vice commissioner of Sichuan, surveillance commissioner of Huguang, and left and right administration commissioner of Zhejiang and Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十年，擢右副都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: In year 20 he was promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 鏓為人持重，有方略。

translations.literal: Zong was dignified in person, with strategic ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was dignified and possessed strategic ability.

sentences.zh: 既蒞重鎮，不上首功。

translations.literal: Once at the vital garrison, he did not report heads for merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once installed at this vital post, he did not inflate merit by reporting enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 一意練步騎，廣儲蓄，繕治關隘亭障，寇為遠徙，俘歸者五百人。

translations.literal: He concentrated on drilling infantry and cavalry, expanding stores, and repairing passes and watchtowers; bandits moved far away and five hundred captives returned.
translations.idiomatic: He concentrated on drilling infantry and cavalry, expanding stores, and repairing passes and watchtowers; the raiders withdrew far away, and five hundred captives returned home.

sentences.zh: 上疏言：「邊將各有常祿，無給田之制。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Frontier generals each have regular salaries; there is no system of granting fields.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Frontier generals each receive regular salaries; there is no system of granting them fields.

sentences.zh: 自武定侯郭勛奏以軍餘開墾田園給將領，委奸軍為莊頭，害殊大。

translations.literal: Since Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun memorialized to open reclaimed fields from army surplus for generals, entrusting wicked soldiers as estate managers—the harm is very great.
translations.idiomatic: Since Marquis of Wuding Guo Xun memorialized to allocate reclaimed land from army surplus to generals and appoint corrupt soldiers as estate managers, the harm has been very great.

sentences.zh: 宜給還軍民，任耕種便。

translations.literal: The fields should be returned to troops and people for convenient cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: The land should be returned to soldiers and civilians for them to farm as they see fit.

sentences.zh: 」帝從其請。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 居數年，引疾歸。

translations.literal: After several years in post, he cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several years in office he cited illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 起故官，撫河南。

translations.literal: He was restored to his former office and pacified Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was restored to his former office and appointed grand coordinator of Henan.

sentences.zh: 尋召為兵部右侍郎，轉左。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as right Vice Minister of War, then transferred to the left.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as vice minister of war (right), then transferred to the left.

sentences.zh: 尚書王以旂出督三邊，鏓署部事。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Yiqi went out to supervise the three frontiers; Zong acted in his stead at the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister Wang Yiqi went out to supervise the three frontiers, Zong acted in his stead at the ministry.

sentences.zh: 頃之，奉詔總理邊關厄隘。

translations.literal: Before long, by imperial order he took overall charge of strategic passes on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, by imperial order he took overall charge of strategic passes on the borders.

sentences.zh: 奏上經略潮河川、居庸關諸處事宜，請於古道門外蜂窩嶺增墩臺一為外屏，浚濠設橋，以防沖突。

translations.literal: He memorialized plans for Chaoxi River, Juyong Pass and other places, asking outside Ancient Road Gate at Fengwo Ridge to add one watch tower as outer screen, dredge moats and set bridges to guard against sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on plans for the Chaoxi River, Juyong Pass, and other places, asking that one watchtower be added outside Ancient Road Gate at Fengwo Ridge as an outer screen, that moats be dredged and bridges set, to guard against sudden assault.

sentences.zh: 川西南兩山對處，各設敵臺，以控中流，分戍兵番直守要害。

translations.literal: Where two mountains face each other southwest of the river, on each set an enemy tower to control midstream; divide garrison troops in rotation to guard vital points.
translations.idiomatic: Where two mountains face each other southwest of the river, enemy towers should be set on each side to control the midstream, with garrison troops rotated in shifts to guard the vital points.

sentences.zh: 又薊鎮五里垛、劃車、開連口、慕田谷等地，宜設墩臺。

translations.literal: Also at Jizhou garrison's Wuliduo, Huache, Kailiankou, Mutian Valley and other places, watch towers should be set.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuliduo, Huache, Kailiankou, Mutian Valley, and other places in the Jizhou garrison, watchtowers should also be built.

sentences.zh: 惡谷、紅土谷、香爐石等地，宜斬崖塹。

translations.literal: At Egu, Hongtugu, Xianglushi and other places, cliffs should be cut and trenches dug.
translations.idiomatic: At Egu, Hongtugu, Xianglushi, and other places, cliffs should be cut and trenches dug.

sentences.zh: 居庸關外諸口，在宣府為內地，在居庸則為邊藩，宜敕東中路文武臣修築。

translations.literal: Passes outside Juyong—in Xuanfu are interior land, at Juyong are frontier—civil and military officials of the eastern middle route should be ordered to repair.
translations.idiomatic: The passes outside Juyong are interior land from Xuanfu's perspective but frontier territory from Juyong's; civil and military officials of the eastern middle route should be ordered to repair them.

sentences.zh: 加潮河川提督為守備，增副將居庸關，領天壽山、黃花鎮。

translations.literal: Promote the Chaoxi River supervisor to garrison commandant; add a vice commander at Juyong Pass to oversee Tianshou Mountain and Huanghua Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: The Chaoxi River supervisor should be promoted to garrison commandant; a vice commander should be added at Juyong Pass to oversee Tianshou Mountain and Huanghua Garrison.

sentences.zh: 設橫嶺守備，塞懷來路，增置新軍二千余人，資團練。

translations.literal: Establish Hengling garrison commandant to block the Huailai road; add more than two thousand new troops to support militia training.
translations.idiomatic: A Hengling garrison commandant should be established to block the Huailai road, and more than two thousand new troops should be added to support militia training.

sentences.zh: 又議紫荊、倒馬、龍泉等關及山海關、古北口經略事宜，請於紫荊之桑谷，倒馬之中{穴羔}關峪，龍泉之陡石嶺諸要害，創築城垣，增設敵樓營舍。

translations.literal: He also deliberated Zijing, Daoma, Longquan passes and Shanhaiguan, Gubeikou affairs, asking at Zijing's Sanggu, Daoma's Zhonggan Pass ravine, Longquan's Doushi Ridge and other vital points to build walls anew and add enemy towers and barracks.
translations.idiomatic: He also set forth plans for Zijing, Daoma, and Longquan passes and for Shanhaiguan and Gubeikou, asking that walls be built anew and enemy towers and barracks added at such vital points as Sanggu in Zijing, the Zhonggan Pass ravine in Daoma, and Doushi Ridge in Longquan.

sentences.zh: 薊州所轄燕河、太平、馬蘭、密雲四路，修築未竟者，括諸司贖鍰竣之。

translations.literal: Of the four routes under Jizhou—Yanhe, Taiping, Malan, Miyun—where repair was unfinished, gather fines from all offices to complete it.
translations.idiomatic: For the four routes under Jizhou—Yanhe, Taiping, Malan, and Miyun—unfinished repairs should be completed with fines collected from all offices.

sentences.zh: 而浮圖峪、插箭嶺尤為紫荊、倒馬二關沖，移參將分駐石門杜家莊，俾保定總兵駐紫荊。

translations.literal: Futu Valley and Chajian Ridge are especially the thrust of Zijing and Daoma two passes; move the vice commander to station separately at Shimen and Dujiazhuang, and let Baoding regional commander station at Zijing.
translations.idiomatic: Futu Valley and Chajian Ridge are especially the points of thrust for Zijing and Daoma; the vice commander should be moved to station separately at Shimen and Dujiazhuang, and the Baoding regional commander should be stationed at Zijing.

sentences.zh: 薊、遼懸絕千里，移建昌營遊擊於山海關。

translations.literal: Jizhou and Liaodong are a thousand li apart; move Jianchang camp's mobile commander to Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou and Liaodong are a thousand li apart; the Jianchang camp mobile commander should be moved to Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 三屯等營缺軍，應速募，馬不足者補入。

translations.literal: Santun and other camps lack troops and should be quickly recruited; those short of horses should be filled in.
translations.idiomatic: Santun and other camps lack troops and should be recruited quickly; those short of horses should be made up.

sentences.zh: 其常戍之兵介胄不備，量給鎧仗，番上者悉予行糧，毋俾荷戈枵腹。

translations.literal: Standing garrison troops lack armor and helmets—issue armor and weapons as measured; all on rotation give marching rations, lest they bear arms on empty stomachs.
translations.idiomatic: Troops on standing garrison lack armor and helmets—armor and weapons should be issued as needed; all those on rotation should receive marching rations, lest they bear arms on empty stomachs.

sentences.zh: 又言：「諸路緩急，以密雲之分守為最。

translations.literal: He also said: "Among all routes for urgency, Miyun's divisional commander is paramount.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Among all routes for urgency, the Miyun divisional commander is paramount.

sentences.zh: 各關要害，以密雲之迤西為最。

translations.literal: Among pass strongpoints, west of Miyun is paramount.
translations.idiomatic: Among pass strongpoints, the country west of Miyun is paramount.

sentences.zh: 若燕河之冷口，馬蘭之黃崖，太平之榆木嶺、擦崖子，皆所急也。

translations.literal: Such as Yanhe's Lengkou, Malan's Huangya, Taiping's Yumu Ridge and Caiyazi—all are urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Cold Pass on the Yanhe route, Huangya on Malan, Yumu Ridge and Caiyazi on Taiping—all are urgent.

sentences.zh: 宜敕撫鎮督諸將領分各營士馬，兼側近按伏之兵，叠為戰守。

translations.literal: Grand coordinators and regional commanders should be ordered to lead generals in dividing each camp's troops and horses, together with nearby ambush forces, in layered battle and defense.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinators and regional commanders should be ordered to lead the generals in dividing each camp's troops and horses, together with nearby ambush forces, in layered battle-and-defense deployment."

sentences.zh: 」兵部言：「軍戍久，戀土。

translations.literal: " The Ministry of War said: "Troops garrisoned long grow attached to the land.
translations.idiomatic: " The Ministry of War said, "Troops garrisoned long grow attached to the land.

sentences.zh: 猝移置，恐他變。

translations.literal: Sudden transfer would fear other disturbances.
translations.idiomatic: Sudden transfer might provoke other disturbances.

sentences.zh: 莫若山海關增置能將一員，募軍三千屯駐，聽薊、遼撫臣調度，援燕河。

translations.literal: Better to add one capable general at Shanhaiguan, recruit three thousand troops to camp there, and let Jizhou and Liaodong grand coordinators deploy them to relieve Yanhe.
translations.idiomatic: Better to add one capable general at Shanhaiguan, recruit three thousand troops to camp there, and let the Jizhou and Liaodong grand coordinators deploy them to relieve Yanhe.

sentences.zh: 」余如鏓言，下守臣議。

translations.literal: " The remainder followed Zong's words and was sent down to border officials for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: " The remainder followed Zong's proposals and was sent down to border officials for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 帝才鏓甚。

translations.literal: The emperor valued Zong highly.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued Zong highly.

sentences.zh: 會兵部尚書趙廷瑞罷，即命鏓入代。

translations.literal: When Minister Zhao Tingrui was dismissed, Zong was immediately ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Zhao Tingrui was dismissed, Zong was immediately ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 鏓以老辭，且言隨事通變，乏將順之宜。

translations.literal: Zong declined on grounds of age, and said adapting flexibly to events lacked the propriety of yielding to the sovereign's will.
translations.idiomatic: Zong declined on grounds of age, and said that adapting flexibly to events lacked the propriety of yielding to the sovereign's will.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，責鏓不恭，削其籍。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry, rebuked Zong for disrespect, and struck him from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry, rebuked Zong for disrespect, and struck him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 時嚴嵩當國，而鏓本由徐階薦，天下推為長者，惜其去，不以罪。

translations.literal: At the time Yan Song held power; Zong had originally been recommended by Xu Jie; all the realm esteemed him as an elder statesman and regretted his departure without treating it as criminal punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Yan Song held power; Zong had originally been recommended by Xu Jie; the realm esteemed him as an elder statesman and regretted his departure, not treating it as a criminal punishment.

sentences.zh: 然鏓罷，帝召翁萬達，甫至以憂去，丁汝夔代之。

translations.literal: Yet when Zong left, the emperor summoned Weng Wanda; he had just arrived when he left on mourning leave, and Ding Ruokui replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Zong left, the emperor summoned Weng Wanda; he had just arrived when he left on mourning leave, and Ding Ruokui replaced him.

sentences.zh: 明年，諳達逼都城，汝夔遂誅死。

translations.literal: The next year Anda pressed the capital; Ruokui was then executed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Anda pressed the capital, and Ruokui was then executed.

sentences.zh: 而鏓歸久之乃卒。

translations.literal: Zong returned home and died only after a long interval.
translations.idiomatic: Zong returned home and died only after a long interval.

sentences.zh: 隆慶元年復官。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longqing his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longqing his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 王邦瑞，字惟賢，宜陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Bangrui, courtesy name Weixian, was a native of Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangrui, courtesy name Weixian, was a native of Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 早有器識。

translations.literal: From youth he had capacity and discernment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed capacity and discernment.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，山東盜起，上剿寇十四策於知府。

translations.literal: As a student, when bandits rose in Shandong he submitted fourteen stratagems against bandits to the prefect.
translations.idiomatic: As a student, when bandits rose in Shandong he submitted fourteen stratagems against bandits to the prefect.

sentences.zh: 正德十二年成進士。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he passed the palace examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Zhengde he passed the palace examination.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士。

translations.literal: He was made a Hanlin bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor.

sentences.zh: 與王府有連，出為廣德知州。

translations.literal: Connected with a princely house, he was sent out as prefect of Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Connected with a princely house, he was sent out as prefect of Guangde.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，祖憂，去。

translations.literal: At the start of Jiajing, on his grandfather's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jiajing, on his grandfather's mourning he left office.

sentences.zh: 補滁州。

translations.literal: He was reassigned to Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned to Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 屢遷南京吏部郎中，出為陜西提學僉事。

translations.literal: After several promotions he became a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then went out as education intendant of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: After several promotions he became a director in the Nanjing Ministry of Personnel, then went out as education intendant of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 坐歲貢不中式五名以上，貶濱州知州。

translations.literal: Because annual tribute students failing the metropolitan exam exceeded five, he was demoted to prefect of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because more than five annual tribute students failed the metropolitan examination, he was demoted to prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 再遷固原兵備副使。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to vice commissioner for military affairs at Guyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred again to vice commissioner for military affairs at Guyuan.

sentences.zh: 涇、邠巨盜李孟春，流劫河東、西，剿平之。

translations.literal: The great bandit Li Mengchun of Jing and Bin raided east and west of the river; he suppressed and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandit Li Mengchun of Jing and Bin raided east and west of the Yellow River; Bangrui suppressed and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 以祖母憂去。

translations.literal: He left on his grandmother's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He left on his grandmother's mourning.

sentences.zh: 服除，復提學陜西，轉參政。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he again served as education intendant of Shaanxi, then was made administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he again served as education intendant of Shaanxi, then was made administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 母憂解職。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: On his mother's mourning he left office.

sentences.zh: 起擢右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: Recalled and promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-chief, grand coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and promoted to right vice censor-in-chief and grand coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 寇乘冰入犯，設伏敗之。

translations.literal: When bandits invaded on the ice he laid an ambush and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits invaded on the ice he laid an ambush and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 改南京大理卿。

translations.literal: He was changed to chief judge of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to chief judge of the Nanjing Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 未上，召為兵部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Before he took up the post he was summoned as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post he was summoned as vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，進左。

translations.literal: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and advanced to the left.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel and advanced to the left vice ministership.

sentences.zh: 諳達犯都城，命邦瑞總督九門。

translations.literal: When Anda attacked the capital, Bangrui was ordered to command all nine gates.
translations.idiomatic: When Anda attacked the capital, Bangrui was ordered to command all nine gates.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞屯禁軍郭外，以巡捕軍營東、西長安街，大啟郭門，納四郊避寇者。

translations.literal: Bangrui camped the forbidden army outside the walls, posted patrol troops on East and West Chang'an Streets, and opened the city gates wide to admit refugees from the four suburbs fleeing bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui camped the forbidden army outside the walls, posted patrol troops on East and West Chang'an Streets, and opened the city gates wide to admit refugees from the four suburbs fleeing the raiders.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書丁汝夔下獄，命邦瑞攝其事，兼督團營。

translations.literal: When Minister Ding Ruokui was imprisoned, Bangrui was ordered to act in his stead and also supervise the regiment camps.
translations.idiomatic: When Minister of War Ding Ruokui was imprisoned, Bangrui was ordered to act in his stead and also supervise the regiment camps.

sentences.zh: 寇退，請治諸將功罪，且浚九門濠塹，皆報可。

translations.literal: When bandits withdrew he requested that generals' merits and faults be judged, and that the moats and ramparts of the nine gates be dredged—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: When the raiders withdrew he requested that generals' merits and faults be judged and that the moats and ramparts of the nine gates be dredged—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞見營制久弛，極陳其弊。

translations.literal: Bangrui saw that camp regulations had long been lax and set forth the abuses at length.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui saw that camp regulations had long been lax and set forth the abuses at length.

sentences.zh: 遂罷十二團營，悉歸三大營，以鹹寧侯仇鸞統之。

translations.literal: Thereupon the twelve regiment camps were abolished and all returned to the three great camps under Xianning Marquis Qiu Luan.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the twelve regiment camps were abolished and all returned to the three great camps under Xianning Marquis Qiu Luan.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞亦改兵部左侍郎，專督營務。

translations.literal: Bangrui was also changed to left Vice Minister of War, specializing in camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui was also made left vice minister of war, specializing in camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 復條上興革六事。

translations.literal: He again submitted six items for reform.
translations.idiomatic: He again submitted six items for reform.

sentences.zh: 中言宦官典兵，古今大患，請盡撤提督監槍者。

translations.literal: Among them he said eunuchs commanding troops were a great calamity of past and present and asked that all supervisors and gunnery overseers be utterly withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: Among them he said that eunuchs commanding troops were a great calamity of past and present and asked that all supervisors and gunnery overseers be utterly withdrawn.

sentences.zh: 帝報從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and followed this.

sentences.zh: 又舉前編修趙時春、工部主事申旞知兵，並改兵部，分理京營事。

translations.literal: He also recommended former compiler Zhao Shichun and works section director Shen Zhe as knowing warfare, and both were changed to the Ministry of War to manage capital camp affairs separately.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended former compiler Zhao Shichun and works section director Shen Zhe as knowing warfare, and both were transferred to the Ministry of War to manage capital camp affairs separately.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝召兵部尚書翁萬達未至，遲之，遂命邦瑞代。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor summoned Minister Weng Wanda, who had not yet arrived; vexed by the delay, he ordered Bangrui to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor summoned Minister of War Weng Wanda, who had not yet arrived; vexed by the delay, he ordered Bangrui to replace him.

sentences.zh: 條上安攘十二事。

translations.literal: He submitted twelve items on pacification and settlement.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted twelve items on pacification and settlement.

sentences.zh: 仇鸞構邦瑞於帝，帝眷漸移。

translations.literal: Qiu Luan slandered Bangrui to the emperor, and imperial favor gradually shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Luan slandered Bangrui to the emperor, and imperial favor gradually shifted away.

sentences.zh: 會鸞奏革薊州總兵官李鳳鳴、大同總兵官徐玨任，而薦京營副將成勛代鳳鳴，密雲副將徐仁代玨。

translations.literal: When Luan memorialized to remove Jizhou regional commander Li Fengming and Datong regional commander Xu Jue, recommending capital camp deputy Cheng Xun to replace Fengming and Miyun deputy Xu Ren to replace Jue—
translations.idiomatic: When Luan memorialized to remove Jizhou regional commander Li Fengming and Datong regional commander Xu Jue, recommending capital camp deputy Cheng Xun to replace Fengming and Miyun deputy Xu Ren to replace Jue—

sentences.zh: 旨從中下。

translations.literal: The rescript issued from below followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The rescript issued from below followed this.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞言：「朝廷易置將帥，必采之公卿，斷自宸衷，所以慎防杜漸，示臣下不敢專也。

translations.literal: Bangrui said: "When the court changes generals and commanders, it must seek them from among the dukes and ministers and decide from the imperial heart alone—this is how to guard against abuse and show that subordinates may not act on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui said, "When the court changes generals and commanders, it must seek them from among the dukes and ministers and decide from the imperial heart alone—this is how to guard against abuse and show that subordinates may not act on their own.

sentences.zh: 且京營大將與列鎮將不相統攝，何緣京營，乃黜陟各鎮。

translations.literal: Moreover capital camp great generals do not command the generals of the various garrisons—on what ground may the capital camps dismiss and appoint each frontier garrison?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, capital camp great generals do not command the generals of the various garrisons—on what ground may the capital camps dismiss and appoint commanders in each frontier garrison?

sentences.zh: 今曲徇鸞請，臣恐九邊將帥悉奔走托附，非國之福也。

translations.literal: Now to bend to Luan's request—I fear all nine-border generals will rush to curry favor—a blessing this is not for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now to bend to Luan's request—I fear all nine-border generals will rush to curry favor, which would not be a blessing for the state.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，下旨譙讓。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased and issued a rebuking edict.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased and issued a rebuking edict.

sentences.zh: 鸞又欲節制邊將，罷築薊鎮邊垣。

translations.literal: Luan also wished to control frontier generals and halt construction on Jizhou's border wall.
translations.idiomatic: Luan also wished to control frontier generals and halt construction on Jizhou's border wall.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞皆以為不可。

translations.literal: Bangrui held all these impossible.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui held all of these impossible.

sentences.zh: 鸞大憾，益肆讒構。

translations.literal: Luan deeply resented this and redoubled slander.
translations.idiomatic: Luan deeply resented this and redoubled his slander.

sentences.zh: 會邦瑞復陳安攘大計，遂嚴旨落職，以冠帶辦事。

translations.literal: When Bangrui again set forth his great plan for pacification, a stern edict demoted him, permitting him to serve wearing his official cap and belt.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangrui again set forth his great plan for pacification, a stern edict demoted him, permitting him to serve while wearing his official cap and belt.

sentences.zh: 居數日，大計自陳。

translations.literal: After several days he himself memorialized his grand plan.
translations.idiomatic: After several days he himself memorialized at the grand evaluation.

sentences.zh: 竟除名，以趙錦代。

translations.literal: In the end his name was removed and Zhao Jin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his name was removed from the rolls and Zhao Jin replaced him.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞去，鸞益橫。

translations.literal: When Bangrui departed Luan grew still more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangrui departed, Luan grew still more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 明年誅死，錦亦坐黨比遣戍，於是帝漸思之。

translations.literal: The next year he was executed; Jin also suffered exile as a partisan—in consequence the emperor gradually came to think of Bangrui.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Luan was executed; Jin was also exiled as a partisan—in consequence the emperor gradually came to think of Bangrui.

sentences.zh: 逾十年，京營缺人，帝曰：「非邦瑞不可。

translations.literal: More than ten years later, when the capital camp lacked a man, the emperor said: "Bangrui alone will do.
translations.idiomatic: More than ten years later, when the capital camp lacked a man, the emperor said, "Bangrui alone will do.

sentences.zh: 」乃起故官。

translations.literal: " He was then recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: " He was then recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 既至，疏便宜數事，悉允行。

translations.literal: Once arrived he memorialized several practical items, all approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived he memorialized several practical items, all of which were approved and carried out.

sentences.zh: 逾年卒。

translations.literal: After a year more he died.
translations.idiomatic: After a year more he died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子少保，謚襄毅，遣行人護喪歸葬。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted the title Xiangyi, and an emissary was sent to escort the coffin home for burial.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made junior guardian of the heir apparent, granted the posthumous title Xiangyi (Resolute and Steadfast), and an emissary was sent to escort the coffin home for burial.

sentences.zh: 邦瑞嚴毅有識量。

translations.literal: Bangrui was stern and resolute, with capacity and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Bangrui was stern and resolute, with capacity and judgment.

sentences.zh: 歷官四十年，以廉節著。

translations.literal: Forty years in office, he was noted for integrity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Over forty years in office he was noted for integrity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 子正國，南京刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhengguo became Vice Minister of Justice at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhengguo became vice minister of justice at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 鄭曉，字窒甫，海鹽人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xiao, courtesy name Zhifu, was a native of Haiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xiao, courtesy name Zhifu, was a native of Haiyan.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年舉鄉試第一。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing he placed first in the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing he placed first in the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 明年成進士，授職方主事。

translations.literal: The next year he passed the palace examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he passed the palace examination and was appointed a director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 日披故牘，盡知天下厄塞、士馬虛實、強弱之數。

translations.literal: Daily he pored over old archives until he knew thoroughly the strategic chokepoints of the realm, the strength and weakness of troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Daily he pored over old archives until he knew thoroughly the strategic chokepoints of the realm and the strength and weakness of troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 尚書金獻民屬撰《九邊圖志》，人爭傳寫之。

translations.literal: Minister Jin Xianmin commissioned him to compile the Record of the Nine Frontiers; people competed to copy it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Jin Xianmin commissioned him to compile the Record of the Nine Frontiers, and people competed to copy it.

sentences.zh: 以爭「大禮」廷杖。

translations.literal: For protesting the Great Rites at court he was beaten with the court cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: For protesting the Great Rites at court he was beaten with the court cudgel.

sentences.zh: 大同兵變，上疏極言不可赦。

translations.literal: When Datong troops mutinied he memorialized strongly that they must not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When Datong troops mutinied he memorialized strongly that they must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 張孚敬柄政，器之，欲改置翰林及言路，曉皆不應。

translations.literal: Zhang Fuzhen held power and valued him, wishing to transfer him to the Hanlin and the remonstrance circuit; Xiao would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fuzhen held power and valued him, wishing to transfer him to the Hanlin Academy and the remonstrance circuit; Xiao would not agree.

sentences.zh: 父憂，歸，久之不起。

translations.literal: On his father's mourning he returned home and for a long time did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: On his father's mourning he returned home and for a long time did not take office.

sentences.zh: 許讃為吏部尚書，調之吏部。

translations.literal: Xu Zan as Minister of Personnel transferred him to that ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zan, as minister of personnel, transferred him to that ministry.

sentences.zh: 歷考功郎中。

translations.literal: He served as director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit-review bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director in the Ministry of Personnel's merit-review bureau.

sentences.zh: 夏言罷相，帝惡言官不糾劾，詔考察去留。

translations.literal: Xia Yan was dismissed as chief minister; the emperor hated that remonstrating officials did not impeach; an edict ordered merit review for retention or dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia Yan was dismissed as chief minister, the emperor resented that remonstrating officials had failed to impeach him and ordered a merit review to decide who should remain in office.

sentences.zh: 大學士嚴嵩因欲去所不悅者，而曉去喬佑等十三人，多嵩所厚。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Yan Song, wishing to remove those he disliked, had Xiao dismiss Qiao You and thirteen others—most of whom Song favored.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Yan Song, wishing to remove officials he disliked, arranged for Xiao to dismiss Qiao You and thirteen others—most of whom Song favored.

sentences.zh: 嵩大憾曉，調文選。

translations.literal: Song greatly resented Xiao and transferred him to the civil appointment bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Song deeply resented Xiao and transferred him to the civil appointment bureau.

sentences.zh: 嵩欲用趙文華為考功，曉言於讃曰：「昔黃禎為文選，調李開先考功，皆山東人，詔不許。

translations.literal: Song wished to use Zhao Wenhua for merit review; Xiao said to Zan: "Formerly Huang Zhen was in civil appointment and transferred Li Kaixian to merit review—both were Shandong men, and an edict forbade it.
translations.idiomatic: Song wished to appoint Zhao Wenhua to merit review; Xiao told Zan, "Formerly Huang Zhen held civil appointment and transferred Li Kaixian to merit review—both were from Shandong, and an edict forbade it.

sentences.zh: 今調文華，曉避位而已。

translations.literal: Now transferring Wenhua—Xiao yields the post, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: If Wenhua is transferred now, I am simply yielding the post.

sentences.zh: 」讃以謝嵩。

translations.literal: " Zan used this to decline Song's request.
translations.idiomatic: " Zan used this to decline Song's request.

sentences.zh: 嵩欲以子世蕃為尚寶丞，曉曰：「治中遷知府，例也。

translations.literal: Song wished to make his son Shifan an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Seals; Xiao said: "From administration vice commissioner to prefect is precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Song wished to make his son Shifan an assistant director of the Court of Imperial Seals; Xiao said, "Promotion from administration vice commissioner to prefect is standard precedent.

sentences.zh: 遷尚寶丞，無故事。

translations.literal: Promotion to assistant director of Imperial Seals has no precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Promotion to assistant director of Imperial Seals has no precedent.

sentences.zh: 」嵩益怒。

translations.literal: " Song grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: " Song grew even angrier.

sentences.zh: 以推謫降官周鈇等，貶曉和州同知。

translations.literal: On the pretext of recommending demoted officials Zhou Fu and others, he demoted Xiao to administration vice commissioner of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the pretext of recommending demoted officials such as Zhou Fu, he demoted Xiao to administration vice commissioner of Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 稍遷太仆丞，歷南京太常卿。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, then served as Minister of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was gradually promoted to vice director of the Court of the Imperial Stud and later served as minister of imperial sacrifices at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 召拜刑部右侍郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Right Vice Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed right vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 俄改兵部，兼副都御史總督漕運。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to the Ministry of War, concurrently Vice Censor-in-chief supervising grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Ministry of War, concurrently serving as vice censor-in-chief supervising grain transport.

sentences.zh: 大江南北皆中倭，漕艘幾阻。

translations.literal: North and south of the Yangzi were all struck by Japanese pirates; grain-transport vessels were nearly blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Japanese raiders struck throughout the lands north and south of the Yangzi, and grain-transport vessels were nearly cut off.

sentences.zh: 曉請發帑金數十萬，造戰舸，築城堡，練兵將，積芻糗。

translations.literal: Xiao asked to issue several hundred thousand taels from the treasury to build war junks, erect forts and castles, train officers and soldiers, and stock fodder and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao asked to issue several hundred thousand taels from the treasury to build war junks, erect forts, train troops, and stock fodder and grain.

sentences.zh: 詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his request.

sentences.zh: 中國奸民利倭賄，多與通。

translations.literal: Chinese traitors profited from Japanese bribes and many communicated with them.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese traitors profited from Japanese bribes, and many colluded with the raiders.

sentences.zh: 通州人顧表者尤桀黠，為倭導。

translations.literal: A Tongzhou man named Gu Biao was especially fierce and cunning and served as guide for the Japanese.
translations.idiomatic: A Tongzhou man named Gu Biao was especially fierce and cunning and served as a guide for the Japanese.

sentences.zh: 以故營寨皆據要害，盡知官兵虛實。

translations.literal: For this reason their camps all held strategic points and knew fully the strengths and weaknesses of government troops.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason their camps held every strategic point and they knew the government's military strengths and weaknesses in full.

sentences.zh: 曉懸重賞捕戮之。

translations.literal: Xiao offered a heavy reward for his capture and execution.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao offered a heavy reward for his capture and execution.

sentences.zh: 募鹽徒驍悍者為兵，增設泰州海防副使，築瓜洲城，廟灣、麻洋、雲梯諸海口皆增兵設堠。

translations.literal: He recruited fierce salt smugglers as soldiers, added a Taizhou coastal defense vice commissioner, walled Guazhou, and at Miaowan, Mayang, Yunti and other estuaries all increased troops and set beacon mounds.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited fierce salt smugglers as soldiers, added a Taizhou coastal defense vice commissioner, walled Guazhou, and reinforced Miaowan, Mayang, Yunti, and other estuaries with troops and beacon mounds.

sentences.zh: 遂破倭於通州，連敗之如臯、海門，襲其軍呂泗，圍之狼山，前後斬首九百余。

translations.literal: He then defeated the Japanese at Tongzhou, repeatedly defeated them at Rugao and Haimen, raided their army at Lüsi, besieged them at Langshan, and in all beheaded more than nine hundred.
translations.idiomatic: He then defeated the Japanese at Tongzhou, repeatedly routed them at Rugao and Haimen, raided their forces at Lüsi, besieged them at Langshan, and took more than nine hundred heads in all.

sentences.zh: 賊潰去。

translations.literal: The bandits collapsed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders collapsed and fled.

sentences.zh: 錄功，再增秩，三賚銀幣。

translations.literal: Merit was recorded; his rank was again raised; three times he was rewarded with silver and silks.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was recorded, his rank was raised again, and he was rewarded with silver and silks three times.

sentences.zh: 時賊多中國人。

translations.literal: At the time most of the bandits were Chinese.
translations.idiomatic: At the time most of the raiders were Chinese.

sentences.zh: 曉言：「武健才谞之徒。

translations.literal: Xiao said: "Men of martial vigor and talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao said, "Men of martial vigor and talent.

sentences.zh: 困無所逞，甘心作賊。

translations.literal: Trapped with no outlet, willingly become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Trapped with no outlet for their abilities, they willingly turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 非國家廣行網羅，使有出身之階，恐有如孫恩、盧循輩出乎其間，禍滋大矣。

translations.literal: Unless the state broadly casts its net and gives them paths to advancement, I fear men like Sun En and Lu Xun may arise among them, and disaster grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the state broadly recruits them and provides paths to advancement, I fear men like Sun En and Lu Xun may arise among them, and the disaster will grow far worse.

sentences.zh: 洪武時倭寇近海州縣。

translations.literal: In Hongwu times Japanese pirates approached coastal prefectures and counties.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hongwu reign Japanese pirates approached coastal prefectures and counties.

sentences.zh: 以高皇帝威靈，兼謀臣宿將，築城練兵，經略數年，猶未乂安。

translations.literal: By the August Emperor's majesty, together with strategists and veteran generals, they walled cities and trained troops; after several years of planning, still it was not fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Even with the August Emperor's majesty, together with strategists and veteran generals, building walls and training troops over several years of planning, the coast was still not fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 乃招漁丁、島人、鹽徒、蜑戶籍為水軍至數萬人，又遣使出海宣布威德。

translations.literal: They then recruited fishermen, islanders, salt smugglers, and boat people into the naval registers to tens of thousands, and also sent envoys overseas to proclaim majesty and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They then enrolled fishermen, islanders, salt smugglers, and boat people as naval forces numbering tens of thousands, and sent envoys overseas to proclaim imperial majesty and virtue.

sentences.zh: 久之，倭始不為患。

translations.literal: After a long time the Japanese ceased to be a affliction.
translations.idiomatic: Only after a long time did the Japanese cease to be a menace.

sentences.zh: 今江北雖平，而風帆出沒，倏忽千里。

translations.literal: Now though the north of the Yangzi is pacified, sails appear and vanish, in an instant a thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Now, though the north of the Yangzi is pacified, enemy sails appear and vanish across a thousand li in an instant.

sentences.zh: 倭恃華人為耳目，華人借倭為爪牙，非詳為區畫，後患未易弭也。

translations.literal: The Japanese rely on Chinese as eyes and ears; Chinese borrow the Japanese as claws and teeth—unless carefully planned in detail, later troubles will not be easily quelled.
translations.idiomatic: The Japanese rely on Chinese as their eyes and ears, while Chinese use the Japanese as their claws and teeth—unless we plan carefully, later troubles will not be easily quelled.

sentences.zh: 」帝頗采納之。

translations.literal: " The emperor largely adopted his views.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 尋召為吏部左侍郎，遷南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as Left Vice Minister of Personnel, then transferred to Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as left vice minister of personnel, then appointed minister of personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 帝以曉知兵，改右都御史協理戎政。

translations.literal: The emperor, because Xiao understood military affairs, changed him to Right Censor-in-chief to assist in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor knew Xiao understood military affairs, he appointed him right censor-in-chief to assist in military administration.

sentences.zh: 尋拜刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 諳達圍大同右衛急，帝命兵部尚書楊博往督大師，乃以曉攝兵部。

translations.literal: Anda's siege of Datong Right Guard was urgent; the emperor ordered Minister of War Yang Bo to go supervise the great army, and had Xiao act for the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: When Anda urgently besieged Datong Right Guard, the emperor ordered Minister of War Yang Bo to supervise the main army and had Xiao act in his stead at the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 曉言：「今兵事方棘，而所簡聽征京軍三萬五千人，乃令執役赴工，何以備戰守？

translations.literal: Xiao said: "Now military affairs are critical, yet of the thirty-five thousand capital troops selected for campaign, they are ordered to labor at construction—how can they prepare for war and defense?
translations.idiomatic: Xiao said, "Military affairs are critical, yet of the thirty-five thousand capital troops selected for campaign, they are being sent to labor on construction projects—how can they prepare for war and defense?

sentences.zh: 乞歸之營伍。

translations.literal: I beg that they be returned to their companies.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that they be returned to their units.

sentences.zh: 」帝立從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately followed this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋還視刑部事。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to oversee Ministry of Justice affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he returned to oversee affairs at the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 嚴嵩勢益熾。

translations.literal: Yan Song's power grew ever more fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Song's power grew ever stronger.

sentences.zh: 曉素不善嵩。

translations.literal: Xiao had never been on good terms with Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao had never been on good terms with Song.

sentences.zh: 而其時大獄如總督王忬以失律，中允郭希顏以言事，曉並予輕比，嵩則置重典。

translations.literal: Yet at that time in great cases such as Grand Coordinator Wang Yu for violation of regulations and Middle Assistant Guo Xiyan for remonstrance, Xiao all applied light analogies while Song imposed heavy statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in major cases such as Grand Coordinator Wang Yu's violation of military regulations and Middle Assistant Guo Xiyan's remonstrance, Xiao applied lenient sentences while Song imposed harsh ones.

sentences.zh: 南都叛卒周山等殺侍郎黃懋官，海寇汪直通倭為亂，曉置重典，嵩故寬假之。

translations.literal: Southern Capital mutineers Zhou Shan and others killed Vice Minister Huang Maoguan; sea bandit Wang Zhi communicated with Japanese to make rebellion—Xiao imposed heavy statutes while Song deliberately showed leniency.
translations.idiomatic: When Southern Capital mutineers led by Zhou Shan killed Vice Minister Huang Maoguan, and sea bandit Wang Zhi colluded with the Japanese in rebellion, Xiao imposed harsh sentences while Song deliberately showed leniency.

sentences.zh: 惟巡撫阮鶚、總督楊順、御史路楷，以嵩曲庇，曉不能盡法，議者譏其失出雲。

translations.literal: Only Grand Coordinators Ruan E and Yang Shun and Investigating Censor Lu Kai, because Song sheltered them crookedly, Xiao could not apply the law fully—critics mocked that his errors exceeded his merits.
translations.idiomatic: Only in the cases of Grand Coordinator Ruan E, Grand Coordinator Yang Shun, and Investigating Censor Lu Kai—whom Song protected—could Xiao not apply the law fully; critics mocked that his failures outweighed his merits.

sentences.zh: 故事，在京軍民訟，俱投牒通政司送法司問斷。

translations.literal: By precedent, lawsuits of soldiers and civilians in the capital all submitted petitions to the Court of Transmission for delivery to the judiciary for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, lawsuits involving soldiers and civilians in the capital were submitted to the Court of Transmission and referred to the judiciary for judgment.

sentences.zh: 諸司有應鞫者，亦參送法司，無自決遣者。

translations.literal: When various offices had cases requiring trial, they also referred them to the judiciary; none decided and dispatched on their own.
translations.idiomatic: When various offices had cases requiring trial, they also referred them to the judiciary; none decided cases on their own authority.

sentences.zh: 後諸司不復遵守，獄訟紛拿。

translations.literal: Later the various offices no longer observed this; prison lawsuits became tangled.
translations.idiomatic: Later the various offices ceased to observe this practice, and legal cases became hopelessly tangled.

sentences.zh: 曉奏循故事，帝報許，於是刑部間捕囚畿府。

translations.literal: Xiao memorialized to follow precedent; the emperor approved; thereupon the Ministry of Justice intermittently arrested prisoners in the capital districts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao memorialized to restore the old practice; the emperor approved, and the Ministry of Justice again began arresting prisoners in the capital districts.

sentences.zh: 而巡按御史鄭存仁謂訟當自下而上，檄州縣，法司有追取，毋輒發。

translations.literal: But investigating censor Zheng Cunren said lawsuits ought to go from lower to higher; he dispatched orders to prefectures and counties that when the judiciary sought persons, they should not be sent forth rashly.
translations.idiomatic: But investigating censor Zheng Cunren argued that lawsuits ought to proceed from lower to higher levels; he ordered prefectures and counties not to release prisoners when the judiciary sought them.

sentences.zh: 曉聞，率侍郎趙大祐、傅頤守故事爭，存仁亦據律執奏。

translations.literal: Xiao heard and led Vice Ministers Zhao Dayou and Fu Yi in upholding precedent in dispute; Cunren also memorialized holding to the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao heard of this, he led Vice Ministers Zhao Dayou and Fu Yi in upholding precedent in protest; Cunren also memorialized citing the statutes.

sentences.zh: 章俱下都察院會刑科平議。

translations.literal: The memorials were all sent down to the Censorate to meet with the penal review section for balanced deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Both memorials were referred to the Censorate and the penal review section for joint deliberation.

sentences.zh: 議未上，曉疏辨。

translations.literal: Before deliberation was submitted, Xiao memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before the deliberation was submitted, Xiao memorialized in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 嵩激帝怒切讓，遂落曉職，兩侍郎亦貶二秩。

translations.literal: Song incited the emperor's anger into sharp rebuke; Xiao was then dismissed from office, and the two vice ministers were also demoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Song incited the emperor's anger into a sharp rebuke; Xiao was dismissed from office, and the two vice ministers were demoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 曉通經術，習國家典故，時望蔚然。

translations.literal: Xiao mastered the classics, was versed in state precedents, and his contemporary reputation was luxuriant.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao mastered the classics, was versed in state precedents, and enjoyed a towering reputation among his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 為權貴所扼，誌不盡行。

translations.literal: Checked by powerful favorites, his aims were not fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Thwarted by powerful favorites, he could not fully carry out his aims.

sentences.zh: 既歸，角巾布衣與鄉里父老遊處，見者不知其貴人也。

translations.literal: After returning, in kerchief and plain cloth he associated with village elders; those who saw him did not know he was a noble man.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home, he wore a scholar's kerchief and plain clothes and mingled with village elders; those who met him did not know he was a man of high rank.

sentences.zh: 既卒，子履淳等訟曉禦倭功於朝，詔復職。

translations.literal: After he died, his son Lüchun and others petitioned at court regarding Xiao's merit in resisting the Japanese; an edict restored his office.
translations.idiomatic: After his death, his son Lüchun and others petitioned the court regarding Xiao's merit in resisting the Japanese; an edict restored his office posthumously.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，贈太子少保，謚端簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longqing he was posthumously made Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and granted the title Duanjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Longqing reign he was posthumously made junior tutor of the heir apparent and granted the title Duanjian (Upright and Simple).

sentences.zh: 履淳自有傳。

translations.literal: Lüchun has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Lüchun has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：李鉞諸人皆以威略幹濟顯於時。

translations.literal: The appraiser says: Li Yue and the others all by martial strategy and practical achievement stood out in their time.
translations.idiomatic: The appraiser says: Li Yue and the others all distinguished themselves in their time through martial prowess and practical achievement.

sentences.zh: 鉞與王憲、王以旂之治軍旅，李承勛、范鏓之畫邊計，才力均有過人者。

translations.literal: Yue together with Wang Xian and Wang Yiqi in governing armies, Li Chengxun and Fan Zong in planning border strategy—all had talent and strength surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: In governing armies, Yue together with Wang Xian and Wang Yiqi; in planning border strategy, Li Chengxun and Fan Zong—all possessed talent and strength surpassing ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 胡世寧奮不顧身，首發奸逆，危言正色，始終一節。

translations.literal: Hu Shining exerted himself without regard for his person, first exposing treachery and rebellion, spoke alarming words with upright countenance, and from beginning to end held to one principle.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Shining risked his life without hesitation, was first to expose treachery and rebellion, spoke alarming truths with an upright bearing, and held to one principle from beginning to end.

sentences.zh: 《易》稱「王臣蹇蹇」，世寧近之矣。

translations.literal: The Changes says "the king's ministers are strenuous"—Shining approached this.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes speaks of "the king's ministers striving strenuously"—Shining came close to that ideal.

sentences.zh: 王邦瑞抵抗權幸，躓而復起，鄭曉諳悉掌故，博洽多聞，兼資文武，所在著效，亦不愧名臣雲。

translations.literal: Wang Bangrui resisted powerful favorites, stumbled yet rose again; Zheng Xiao was thoroughly versed in administrative precedents, broadly learned and well informed, combined civil and military qualifications, wherever he served showed achievement—also not unworthy of the name great minister.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Bangrui resisted powerful favorites, stumbled yet rose again; Zheng Xiao was thoroughly versed in administrative precedents, broadly learned, and combined civil and military talents—wherever he served he achieved results and was no unworthy of the name great minister.
